questions.rankerTip: Asymptotes are tangents to the hyperbola at infinity, intersecting at the center of the hyperbola.
questions.topic: Basic Engineering Drawing - Curves - Hyperbola & Asymptotes

questions.question: If a line is parallel to any one of the reference planes and inclined to the other then:
options: Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true length
Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true inclination
questions.explanation: If a line is parallel to a plane of projection, its projection on that plane will faithfully show both its true length and its true inclination to the other reference plane.
questions.rankerTip: Line parallel to a plane shows BOTH true length AND true inclination on that plane.
questions.topic: Basic Engineering Drawing - Projections - Lines Parallel to One Plane

questions.question: The continuous thin ruled lines with short zig-zags within them are drawn to show:
questions.explanation: According to IS 10714 (Type D line), a continuous thin straight line with short zig-zags is designated to represent long break lines or limits of partial/interrupted views. Continuous wavy freehand lines (Type C) are used for short break lines.
questions.rankerTip: Continuous thin with zig-zag (Type D) = Long break lines; Continuous thin wavy (Type C) = Short break lines.
questions.topic: Basic Engineering Drawing - Lines - Break Lines (Type C & D)

questions.question: Which field book is convenient for large scale and detailed dimension work?
questions.explanation: A single-line field book provides wider sketching space on either side of the single central red line, making it much more convenient for large-scale work where extensive dimensions and details must be entered.
questions.rankerTip: Single line = large scale and detailed dimensions. Double line = ordinary engineering & cadastral surveys.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Field Book Types

questions.question: A well-conditioned triangle does not have any angle less than:
questions.explanation: A well-conditioned triangle should not have any angle less than 30° nor greater than 120° to avoid errors during intersection plotting.
questions.rankerTip: Angles must lie strictly between 30° and 120°. Ideal triangle is equilateral (60° each).
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Triangulation & Triangles

questions.question: Invar tape is made up of an alloy of
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "36% Nickel and 64% Steel". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Invar Tape.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #14 on Invar Tape.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Invar Tape

questions.question: What is the term for error that occur due to faulty adjustments of device such as chain may be too long or too short?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (D): "Instrumental error". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Errors in Chaining.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #34 on Errors in Chaining.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Errors in Chaining

questions.question: Metric chains are generally available in :
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (C): "20 m and 30 m length". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Metric Chain.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #53 on Metric Chain.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Metric Chain

questions.question: In chain survey reference sketches are used
options: To mark readings during survey work
To locate survey stations on future date
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (D): "To locate survey stations on future date". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Reference Sketches.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #73 on Reference Sketches.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Reference Sketches

questions.question: What is the term that the distance measured at right angles to the chain line from the object?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (D): "Perpendicular off set". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Offsets.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #92 on Offsets.

questions.question: Which sign is used to indicate tie or subsidiary station?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (C): "ÿ". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Survey Station Symbols.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #111 on Survey Station Symbols.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Survey Station Symbols

questions.question: The Principle of chain surveying is
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "Triangulation". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Survey Principles.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #131 on Survey Principles.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Survey Principles

questions.question: Direct ranging is possible only when the end points are :
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "Mutually inter visible". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Direct Ranging.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #150 on Direct Ranging.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Direct Ranging

questions.question: Permissible error in chaining for measurement on a hilly ground is
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (A): "1 : 250". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Permissible Errors.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #170 on Permissible Errors.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Permissible Errors

questions.question: What is the length if metallic tape available in meter?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (D): "15m and 30m". High-yield Kerala PSC Chain Survey standard syllabus question on Metallic Tape.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Question #189 on Metallic Tape.
questions.topic: Chain Survey - Chain Survey - Metallic Tape

questions.question: All revenue survey maps are plotted with reference to the.... meridian
questions.explanation: True meridian lines remain constant and permanent over time (independent of magnetic declination variations). Therefore, government revenue survey maps and cadastral boundaries are invariably plotted with reference to the True Meridian.
questions.rankerTip: Revenue survey maps and permanent cadastral boundaries are always plotted with reference to the True Meridian.

questions.question: On the graduated ring of the prismatic compass 90° is marked at ......end of needle
questions.explanation: Graduations on a prismatic compass ring run clockwise from South (0°). Therefore: South = 0°/360°, West = 90°, North = 180°, East = 270°.
questions.rankerTip: In Prismatic Compass, 90° is at the West end, NOT East.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Prismatic Compass

questions.question: Extent of diurnal variation of magnetic declination
options: greater at the equator and less at the poles
less at the equator and greater at the poles
same at both equator and at the poles
does not depend on the locality
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "less at the equator and greater at the poles". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Diurnal Variation.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #7 on Diurnal Variation.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Diurnal Variation

questions.question: The fore bearing of a line is S 45°10' E find the back bearing
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "N 45°-10' W". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Back Bearing.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #23 on Back Bearing.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Back Bearing

questions.question: In whole circle system, the back bearing of a line is equal to :
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (C): "FB ± 180°". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Back Bearing Formula.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #39 on Back Bearing Formula.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Back Bearing Formula

questions.question: The graduated ring of a prismatic compass is graduated in
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "Whole circle bearing system". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Whole Circle Bearing System.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #55 on Whole Circle Bearing System.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Whole Circle Bearing System

questions.question: The total number of zeros graduated on surveyor's compass is
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (B): "Two". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Surveyor's Compass Graduations.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #71 on Surveyor's Compass Graduations.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Surveyor's Compass Graduations

questions.question: When the declination is negative, the magnetic meridian will be on which side of true meridian
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (A): "Western". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Magnetic Declination.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #87 on Magnetic Declination.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Magnetic Declination

questions.question: What is the name of instrument, to measure the bearing line in quadrantal system?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (D): "Surveyor's compass". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Surveyor's Compass.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #103 on Surveyor's Compass.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Surveyor's Compass

questions.question: The reduced bearing may have any values between :
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (A): "0° and 90°". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Reduced Bearing Range.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #119 on Reduced Bearing Range.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Reduced Bearing Range

questions.question: The lines of earth's magnetic field run from
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (C): "North to south". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Magnetic Field Lines.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #135 on Magnetic Field Lines.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Magnetic Field Lines

questions.question: What is the variation, in the magnetic meridian swings like a pendulum in one direction for a long period and gradually comes to rest and then swings in the opposite direction?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option (A): "Secular variation". High-yield Kerala PSC Compass Survey standard syllabus question on Secular Variation.
questions.rankerTip: Kerala PSC Repeated Compass Question #151 on Secular Variation.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Compass Survey - Secular Variation

questions.question: Orientation by ___ is the most accurate method of orientation and is always to preferred.
questions.explanation: In plane table surveying, orientation by back-sighting (sighting along a previously drawn ray to a known preceding station) is the most accurate and reliable method because it is completely unaffected by local magnetic variations or metallic disturbances.
questions.rankerTip: Orientation by backsighting is the most accurate method of orientation and is always preferred over magnetic orientation.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Planetable Survey - Orientation Methods

questions.question: Which of the following is not a methodology for the solution of a three-point problem ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Kirchhoff's method'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Kirchhoff's method.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Plane Table Surveying Principles

questions.question: The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Radiation'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Radiation.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Plane Table Surveying Principles

questions.question: The best method of solving three point problem is :
questions.explanation: Lehmann's method (Trial and Error method) is the most rapid, commonly used, and accurate field method for solving the Three-Point Problem using Lehmann's rules to eliminate the triangle of error.
questions.rankerTip: Lehmann's method (Trial & Error) = Fastest and most accurate solution to the 3-point problem.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Resection and Three-Point Problem

questions.question: The method chiefly used for locating the details from stations, which have been previously established by triangulation
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Traversing'. In plane tabling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Traversing.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Plane Table Surveying Principles

questions.question: A curved surface which of every point is perpendicular to the direction of gravity at the points is called:
questions.explanation: A level surface is defined as a curved surface on which every point is perpendicular (normal) to the direction of gravity (the plumb line) at that point. A still body of water undisturbed by tides or wind represents a level surface. A horizontal surface, in contrast, is tangential to a level surface at only one point.
questions.rankerTip: Curved surface normal to plumb line at all points = Level surface. Plane tangential at one point = Horizontal surface.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Levelling - Definitions & Terms

questions.question: The direct method of contouring is :
questions.explanation: The direct method of contouring is the most accurate method because points on the actual contour lines are physically located on the ground and surveyed.
questions.rankerTip: Direct method is slow, tedious, and costly, but gives the highest accuracy for small areas.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Methods of Contouring - Direct Method

questions.question: Contour interval for mountainous region is
questions.explanation: For general engineering surveys in hilly/mountainous terrain, a contour interval of 2 m (or 5 m depending on scale) is commonly adopted.
questions.rankerTip: Official answer as per Kerala PSC syllabus: 2 m.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Contour Interval Selection

questions.question: Which method is suitable for the contouring of hilly areas?
questions.explanation: The tacheometric method is the most suitable for contouring steep, broken, or hilly terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible.
questions.rankerTip: Hilly/broken terrain = Tacheometric method.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Contouring Hilly Areas - Tacheometric

questions.question: If the higher values are inside the bend or loop in the contour, it indicates a :
questions.explanation: U-shaped contours with higher values inside the loop indicate a ridge line. V-shaped contours with higher values outside indicate a valley line.
questions.rankerTip: Higher values inside loop = Ridge; Higher values outside loop = Valley.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Ridge vs Valley Contours

questions.question: In the case of overhanging cliffs
options: Two consecutive contours intersect in a contour map
Two consecutive contours coincide each other
questions.explanation: In an overhanging cliff, contours cross/intersect each other because a point on the ground can have two different elevations at the same horizontal coordinate.
questions.rankerTip: Overhanging cliff = Contours intersect / cross each other.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Overhanging Cliff Intersection

questions.question: A reference surface above which elevation of a point are determined is called a ______ surface
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Datum'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Datum.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Levelling Principles and Operations

questions.question: The still water surface of a pond represent a ______ surface
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Levelling Principles and Operations

questions.question: A surface which is normal to the direction of gravity at all points, as indicated by a plumb line, is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Level surface'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Level surface.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Levelling Principles and Operations

questions.question: The vertical distance above or below the datum is ______ of a point.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'The elevation'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: The elevation.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Bench Marks and Datum

questions.question: The sensitiveness of a level tube decreases, if
options: Radius of curvature of its inner surface is increased
Diameter of the tube is increased
Length of the vapour is increased
Both viscosity and surface tension are increased
questions.explanation: Sensitiveness decreases when viscosity and surface tension of the bubble liquid increase, as this impedes smooth bubble movement.
questions.rankerTip: Higher viscosity and surface tension = Decreased bubble sensitiveness.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Level Tube and Sensitiveness

questions.question: Diaphragm of a survey telescope is held inside
options: Telescope tube at its end nearer the eye piece
Telescope tube at its mid point
questions.explanation: The diaphragm holding the crosshairs is fitted inside the telescope tube just in front of the eyepiece, at the focal plane of the objective.
questions.rankerTip: Crosshairs / Diaphragm are fitted directly in front of the eyepiece.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Telescope Components and Optics

questions.question: The stake erected at the required elevation is called :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Grade stake'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Grade stake.
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Levelling Principles and Operations

questions.question: If L is in kilometers, the curvature correction is :
questions.explanation: Curvature correction = D² / (2R) = 0.0785 D² metres (when D is in km), or 78.4 L² mm.
questions.rankerTip: Cc = 0.0785 D² m = 78.4 L² mm (where D or L is in km).
questions.topic: Levelling and Contouring - Curvature and Refraction Corrections

questions.question: How to eliminate parallax between the staff and reticle in auto level?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Turn the focusing knob'. In surveying and levelling, this follows standard Kerala PSC specifications.
questions.rankerTip: Important exam point: Turn the focusing knob.

questions.question: Which method is useful for measuring precisely a number of horizontal angle from a single station point in theodolite instrument:
questions.explanation: The method of reiteration (direction method) is used to measure several angles from a single station by sighting surrounding stations in succession and closing the horizon on the starting station.
questions.rankerTip: Multiple angles from single station = Reiteration (Direction) method.

questions.question: The angle between prolongation of preceding line and the forward line of a traverse is called:
questions.explanation: A deflection angle is the angle that a survey line makes with the prolongation of the preceding survey line. It is designated as right (clockwise) or left (counter-clockwise).
questions.rankerTip: Deflection angles are widely used in open traverse surveying for highways, railways, and pipelines.

questions.question: Face left and face right observations are connected with
questions.explanation: Face left and face right observations are uniquely connected with theodolite observations to eliminate systematic instrumental errors.
questions.rankerTip: Face left & face right = Theodolite surveying technique.
questions.topic: Theodolite Survey - Face Left and Face Right Observations

questions.question: The line passing through the centres of curvature of the faces of lens is known as :
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Principle axis'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Principle axis.
questions.topic: Theodolite Survey - Telescope Optics and Aberrations

questions.question: The vertical circle of the instrument is on the left of the observer while taking a reading the position is called
options: Both Face left observation and Normal position
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Both Face left observation and Normal position'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Both Face left observation and Normal position.
questions.topic: Theodolite Survey - Vertical Circle and Index Error

questions.question: What is the name of theodolite if its telescope can be revolved through 180° in a vertical plane about its horizontal axis?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Transit theodolite'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Transit theodolite.

questions.question: What method is used for imperfect graduations are minimized by reading on different parts of the graduated circle in theodolite?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Repetition method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Repetition method.

questions.question: The face left position is also known as :
questions.explanation: When the vertical circle of the theodolite is on the left side of the observer while sighting, the telescope is in the Face Left (or normal) position.
questions.rankerTip: Vertical circle on observer's LEFT = Face Left / Telescope Normal.
questions.topic: Theodolite Survey - Face Left and Face Right Observations

questions.question: What type of method is the displacement of signal are not eliminated in horizontal measurement?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Repetition method'. In theodolite surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Repetition method.

questions.question: What is the least count of theodolite instrument?
questions.explanation: The least count of a standard engineer's vernier theodolite is 20 seconds (20").
questions.rankerTip: Least count of vernier theodolite = 20" (0' 20").
questions.topic: Theodolite Survey - Theodolite Scales and Least Count

questions.question: Which process is used for the transmission of radio signals from the satellites into the GPS receiver for position determination?
questions.explanation: GPS positioning determines receiver coordinates by measuring pseudo-ranges (distances) from multiple satellites with known coordinates, which is the geometric process of trilateration.
questions.rankerTip: GPS position determination is based on Trilateration (distance intersections), not angular triangulation.

questions.question: What is the shape of single reflector prism?
questions.explanation: Retroreflectors used in surveying are cube corner (corner-cube / trihedral) prisms composed of three mutually perpendicular reflecting faces.
questions.rankerTip: Cube corner (triple prism / retroreflector) reflects light back parallel to its incident direction.
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - Total Station - Prisms & Reflectors

questions.question: An EDM based instrument is
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'Total station'. In modern surveying, this conforms to standard Kerala PSC guidelines.
questions.rankerTip: Key exam takeaway: Total station.
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - Modern Survey Instruments and Total Station

questions.question: EDM stands for :
questions.explanation: EDM stands for Electronic Distance Measurement (or Electronic Distance Meter), an instrument that measures distances using electromagnetic wave propagation.
questions.rankerTip: EDM = Electronic Distance Measurement.
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - EDM Fundamentals and Principles

questions.question: What is the another name of "modulating wave"?
questions.explanation: In EDM theory, the low-frequency wave that carries the measurement wavelength and is superimposed onto the high-frequency optical carrier wave is called the Modulating wave (or Measuring wave).
questions.rankerTip: Modulating wave = Measuring wave.
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - EDM Modulation Principles

questions.question: GPS is owned and operated by
questions.explanation: The Global Positioning System (GPS) is owned, financed, and operated by the United States Government (U.S. Space Force / Department of Defense).
questions.rankerTip: GPS owner and operator: US Government.

questions.question: How many Orbit planes are available for satellites in space segment?
questions.explanation: The GPS space segment constellation consists of satellites distributed across 6 equally spaced orbital planes, each inclined at 55° and separated by 60° on the equator.
questions.rankerTip: Number of GPS orbital planes: 6 planes (with 4+ satellites in each plane).
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - GPS Orbital Planes

questions.question: What are the two types of Planimeter?
questions.explanation: Planimeters are primarily classified into two types: Mechanical Planimeters (e.g., Amsler Polar Planimeter, Roller Planimeter) and Digital / Electronic Planimeters (microprocessor-controlled with digital display).
questions.rankerTip: Two main types of planimeter: Mechanical and Digital.
questions.topic: Modern Survey Instruments - Types of Planimeter

questions.question: The most effective command used to draw symmetrical objects is:
questions.explanation: The MIRROR command (alias MI) creates a reverse/reflected copy of selected objects about a specified mirror line, making it the fastest and most accurate command for drawing symmetrical objects.
questions.rankerTip: MIRROR (MI) command is specifically designed for creating symmetrical drawings across an axis.

questions.question: Shortcut used in AutoCAD for pasting object is:
questions.explanation: Standard Windows shortcut Ctrl + V pastes copied objects into the active drawing. (Ctrl + C is Copy, Ctrl + X is Cut, and Ctrl + P is Plot/Print).
questions.rankerTip: Ctrl + V = Paste, Ctrl + C = Copy to Clipboard, Ctrl + Shift + V = Paste as Block.

questions.question: Shortcut key of single line text is:
questions.explanation: DT (or DTEXT) launches single-line text creation. MT (or T) is for multiline text (MTEXT), and ST is for Text Style.
questions.rankerTip: DT = Single-line Dynamic Text; MT/T = Multiline Text (MTEXT); ST = Text Style dialog.

questions.question: What is the use of the shortcut key Mtext?
questions.explanation: MTEXT (alias MT or T) is used to create multiline text formatted as paragraph blocks with word wrapping.
questions.rankerTip: MTEXT = Multiline Text (formatted paragraphs with formatting ruler).

questions.question: Which command converts discrete object in polyline?
questions.explanation: The JOIN command (alias J) or PEDIT > Join fuses multiple contiguous lines, arcs, or polylines sharing endpoints into a single, continuous 2D Polyline.
questions.rankerTip: JOIN (J) connects contiguous discrete lines/arcs into a single polyline.

questions.question: Function key F10 is used in AutoCAD to:
questions.explanation: Function key F10 toggles Polar Tracking ON/OFF, guiding crosshairs along specified angular increments.
questions.rankerTip: F10 = Polar Tracking ON/OFF (angular guidelines).

questions.question: ..... are the instructions you provide to CAD software to achieve the end result:
questions.explanation: Commands (entered at the command prompt or selected from menus/ribbons) are the fundamental software instructions telling CAD what operation to execute.
questions.rankerTip: Commands are user instructions to CAD software entered via keyboard or UI.

questions.question: ..... command allows to shrink or enlarge the already existing drawing about a base point:
questions.explanation: The SCALE command (alias SC) enlarges or reduces the size of selected objects proportionally about a chosen base point using a scale factor.
questions.rankerTip: SCALE (SC) alters object size proportionally around a base point.

questions.question: 60% of number is 6, Identify the number :
questions.explanation: Let the unknown number be x. (60 / 100) × x = 6 => x = (6 × 100) / 60 = 600 / 60 = 10.
questions.rankerTip: (Part / Percentage) × 100 = Total. Here, (6 / 60) × 100 = 10.

questions.question: What percentage of 80 is 20?
questions.explanation: Required fraction / decimal: 20 / 80 = 1 / 4 = 0.25 (which corresponds to 25%).
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Percentages & Fractions

questions.question: Find 6% of 750.
Two third of the square of a certain number is 96. What is the number ?
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Square Roots & Algebra

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be the unit digit in a perfect square ?
questions.explanation: The square of any integer can only end in {0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9} (0²=0, 1²=1, 2²=4, 3²=9, 4²=6, 5²=5, 6²=6, 7²=9, 8²=4, 9²=1). A perfect square never ends with 2, 3, 7, or 8. Therefore, 7 cannot be the unit digit in a perfect square.
questions.rankerTip: A perfect square NEVER ends in 2, 3, 7, or 8.
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Square Roots & Properties of Numbers
Workshop Calculation and Science - Square Roots & Decimals

questions.question: What will 60% of a number be whose 150% is 120 ?
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Percentages & Proportion

questions.question: If 5 : 4 = 35 : X, then the value of X is :
questions.explanation: In a proportion, product of extremes equals product of means: 5 × X = 4 × 35 => X = (4 × 35) / 5 = 4 × 7 = 28.
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Ratio and Proportion

questions.question: Rs. 250 is divided between Arun and Sasi, and Arun gets 100. Find the ratio of division of the amount.
questions.explanation: Total amount = Rs. 250. Arun's share = Rs. 100. Sasi's share = 250 − 100 = Rs. 150. Ratio of Arun's share to Sasi's share = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Ratio and Proportion

questions.question: The least number of 4 digits which is a perfect square is :
questions.explanation: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000. √1000 ≈ 31.62. The next whole integer is 32. 31² = 961 (a 3-digit number). 32² = 1024 (the first 4-digit number). Hence, 1024 is the least 4-digit perfect square.
questions.rankerTip: 31² = 961 (3 digits), 32² = 1024 (smallest 4-digit perfect square).
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Square Roots & Number Theory

questions.question: One hectare is equivalent to how many square metres?
questions.explanation: 1 hectare = 100 m x 100 m = 10,000 square metres. 1 acre = 4046.86 sq.m or 43,560 sq.ft.
questions.rankerTip: 1 hectare = 2.471 acres. Very common conversion in Land Records revenue work.

questions.question: What is the mechanical advantage (MA) of a simple machine with a load of 1000 N lifted by an effort of 250 N?
questions.explanation: Mechanical Advantage (MA) = Load / Effort = 1000 N / 250 N = 4.
questions.rankerTip: Efficiency = (Mechanical Advantage / Velocity Ratio) x 100%.
questions.topic: Workshop Calculation and Science - Simple Machines

questions.question: Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the:
questions.explanation: Vicat's apparatus is a standard testing instrument used for multiple cement tests: a 10 mm diameter plunger is used for the standard/normal consistency test (P), a 1 mm square needle for the initial setting time test, and an annular collar needle for the final setting time test.
questions.rankerTip: Vicat plunger (10 mm) = Consistency (P); 1 mm square needle = Initial setting; Annular needle = Final setting.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Cement Testing - Vicat Apparatus

questions.question: The heating of limestone to redness in contact with air is known as:
questions.explanation: Calcination is the process of heating limestone (CaCO3) to red heat (approx. 800–900°C) in the presence of air to drive off carbon dioxide, producing quicklime (CaO).
questions.rankerTip: CaCO3 + Heat -> CaO + CO2 is Calcination. CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + Heat is Slaking.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Lime - Calcination & Manufacture

questions.question: The alternate dry and wet conditions causes the development of ... in timber:
questions.explanation: Wet rot is caused by fungi attacking timber subjected to alternate wet and dry environments. Dry rot occurs in warm, damp, and unventilated conditions.
questions.rankerTip: Alternate wet and dry conditions cause Wet Rot. Lack of ventilation with dampness causes Dry Rot.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Timber - Fungal Decay & Wet Rot

questions.question: Which of the following is an igneous rock?
questions.explanation: Basalt is an extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock formed by the cooling of lava on the Earth's surface. (Slate and Gneiss are metamorphic; Kankar is sedimentary).
questions.rankerTip: Igneous: Granite, Basalt, Trap, Diorite, Gabbro. Metamorphic: Marble, Slate, Gneiss, Quartzite. Sedimentary: Limestone, Sandstone, Kankar, Shale.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Stones - Igneous Rocks & Basalt

questions.question: The normal consistency of Portland cement is about:
questions.explanation: Standard consistency (P) of Ordinary Portland Cement typically ranges between 25% and 30% by weight of dry cement.
questions.rankerTip: Standard consistency of OPC ≈ 25% to 30%. Initial & final setting time test uses 0.85P water; Soundness test uses 0.78P water.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Cement - Standard Consistency

questions.question: The main function of alumina in brick earth is:
questions.explanation: Alumina (Al2O3) is the essential ingredient in clay that provides plasticity, enabling the brick earth to be moulded into shape.
questions.rankerTip: Alumina imparts plasticity for moulding. Silica prevents shrinkage, cracking, and warping. Iron oxide gives red color.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Bricks - Composition & Plasticity

questions.question: The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement shall not be:
questions.explanation: As per IS 269 / IS 456, the initial setting time of OPC shall not be less than 30 minutes, and the final setting time shall not exceed 600 minutes (10 hours).
questions.rankerTip: OPC setting times: Initial setting time ≥ 30 minutes; Final setting time ≤ 600 minutes (10 hours).
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Cement - Setting Times (IS 269)

questions.question: The coarseness of the grains of a mineral is known as:
questions.explanation: Texture refers to the size, shape, and mutual arrangement of mineral grains (e.g., fine-grained, coarse-grained, porphyritic).
questions.rankerTip: Texture = grain size and arrangement (fine, medium, coarse-grained). Fracture = surface appearance along a break.
questions.topic: Building Materials and Construction - Stones & Minerals - Texture & Grain Structure

mockTests.title: Kerala PSC Tracer / Surveyor Grade II - 100 MCQ Grand PYQ Exam (Paper 43/2023)
mockTests.description: Authentic 100-mark full syllabus examination paper from Paper 43/2023 for Tracer / Surveyor Grade II across Survey & Land Records, LSGD, and Irrigation departments. Evaluated with standard PSC negative marking (+1.00 / -0.33).
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey and Land Records / LSGD / Irrigation

questions.question: As per BIS (IS 1444-1989) the standard size of B1 drawing board is _________
questions.explanation: Standard drawing board sizes as per BIS (IS 1444-1989): B0 = 1000 × 1500 mm, B1 = 700 × 1000 mm, B2 = 500 × 700 mm, B3 = 350 × 500 mm.

questions.question: For drawing long thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened
questions.explanation: A chisel edge is sharpened to maintain a uniform line thickness along straight edges (ruler/T-square). Conical points wear rapidly and broaden line width.

questions.question: The ratio of length to width of all arrow heads in drawing is
questions.explanation: According to SP 46 / IS 10714 drafting standards, dimension arrowheads must have a standard length-to-width (depth-to-spread) ratio of 3:1.

questions.question: For thin chain line alternate long and short dashes are in proportion ranging from
questions.explanation: For thin chain lines (center lines / Type G), long dashes are 9 to 12 mm and short dashes are 1.5 to 2 mm, giving a proportion ranging from 6:1 to 4:1.

questions.question: The plan and elevation of a line segment are seen coincides, the line is situated in the
questions.explanation: When a line lies in the 2nd quadrant (above HP, behind VP) or 4th quadrant (below HP, in front of VP), upon rotating HP by 90°, the plan (top view) and elevation (front view) overlap on the same side of the reference line XY.

questions.question: The recommended dimensioning of a sphere of Diameter 20 mm is
questions.explanation: As per ISO/BIS drafting conventions, spherical diameter is dimensioned by prefixing the symbol 'S' before the diameter symbol Ø, formatted as S Ø 20 (or SR for spherical radius).

questions.question: The type of Vernier in which the Vernier divisions are marked in the opposite direction of the main scale is
questions.explanation: In a backward (retrograde) vernier, divisions are numbered in the direction opposite to the main scale, where n vernier divisions equal (n + 1) main scale divisions.

questions.question: The method of projection in which the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane the projection is
questions.explanation: Orthographic projection is an axonometric/parallel projection method where projection rays are mutually parallel to each other and normal (perpendicular) to the projection plane.

questions.question: RF = 200:1 represents a
questions.explanation: Representative Fraction (RF) > 1 (e.g. 200:1) indicates an enlarging scale used for small precision components. RF < 1 is a reducing scale.

questions.question: Scale 1 : 200 is classified as
questions.explanation: A scale of 1:200 has an RF < 1, meaning 1 unit on the drawing represents 200 units in reality; it is a reducing scale.

questions.question: The survey in which earth's curvature is taken into account is
questions.explanation: In geodetic surveying, the curvature of the earth's spheroidal surface is taken into account for large areas (> 250 km²).

questions.question: Surveying Chain is Made up of
questions.explanation: Survey chains are manufactured from galvanized mild steel (MS) wire of 4 mm diameter (8 SWG) with ends looped into rings.

questions.question: The Length of surveyor's chain is
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain (surveyor's chain) is 66 feet (20.12 m) long and consists of 100 links, with each link measuring 0.66 ft (7.92 inches).

questions.question: In ordinary chain survey the maximum permissible error is
questions.explanation: In ordinary chain surveying under normal field conditions, the maximum permissible ratio of error is 1 in 1000 (1 in 250 in rough ground; 1 in 1000 is official key for standard ordinary chaining).

questions.question: The correction for sag is always _____
questions.explanation: Correction for sag is always negative (-ve) because the catenary curve makes the measured distance between supports longer than the true straight chord distance.

questions.question: If L is the correct length of a chain, L' is the incorrect length and D' is the measured length, then the correct length is:
questions.explanation: True distance = (Measured length) × (Incorrect length of chain / True length of chain) = D' × (L' / L).

questions.question: The instrument which is not used in chain survey is
questions.explanation: A levelling staff is used exclusively in levelling and tachometric work to measure vertical elevations, not for linear distance measurement in chain surveying.

questions.question: The Principle of chain surveying is
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle of chain surveying is triangulation, whereby the survey area is partitioned into a network of well-conditioned triangles.

questions.question: The system of lines or Triangles covering the area to be surveyed is
questions.explanation: The system of survey lines forming the skeleton network of triangles covering the area to be surveyed is called the framework.

questions.question: In a well-conditioned triangle the angles are
questions.explanation: A well-conditioned triangle has no angle less than 30° and no angle greater than 120° to minimize geometric plotting distortion.

questions.question: The line joining some fixed points termed as tie stations on main survey line is called
questions.explanation: A tie line joins auxiliary (tie) stations on main survey lines to measure offsets for locating interior ground details.

questions.question: Invar tape is made up of an alloy of and steel.
questions.explanation: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy (36% Nickel, 64% Steel) characterized by an exceptionally low coefficient of thermal expansion.

questions.question: The process of establishing an intermediate point in a line is called
questions.explanation: Ranging is the operational process of aligning intermediate points along a straight survey line between two terminal stations.

questions.question: Error =
options: Difference in values and sign of observed value
Difference in values and sign of true value
questions.explanation: By standard definition, Error = Observed Value - True Value (while Correction = True Value - Observed Value = -Error).

questions.question: Of the following, which is the primary stage of surveying ?
questions.explanation: Reconnaissance is the initial ground inspection of the survey area to observe boundaries, terrain features, and select station points.

questions.question: Bad ranging is an example for
questions.explanation: Bad (imperfect) ranging causes the chain to deviate from a true straight line, consistently making the measured length greater than the true length (positive cumulative error).

questions.question: Survey lines set out to locate interior details of a plot is called
questions.explanation: Tie lines are secondary lines run across main survey lines to locate interior ground features and details.

questions.question: A link of a metric chain is cm in length.
questions.explanation: Each link of a standard 20 m or 30 m metric chain measures 0.2 m (20 cm) between the centers of connecting rings.

questions.question: Which of the following is the prime instrument is used for ranging ?
questions.explanation: Ranging rods (typically 2 to 3 m long, octagonal or circular poles painted in alternating red/black and white bands) are the prime tools for visual alignment.

questions.question: A 20 m metric chain has links.
questions.explanation: A 20-meter metric chain consists of 100 links (each link = 20 cm = 0.2 m). A 30 m metric chain has 150 links.

questions.question: 90° is set out using:
questions.explanation: An open cross-staff is used on survey lines to set out right angles (90°) for perpendicular offsets.

questions.question: ___________ angles can be set out using French cross staff.
questions.explanation: An octagonal French cross staff has sighting slits set at angles that allow setting out both 45° and 90° lines.

questions.question: Gunter's chain is ___________ in length.
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain (surveyor's chain) is 66 feet long and contains 100 links (1 link = 0.66 ft = 7.92 in).

questions.question: Survey related to large water bodies is called
questions.explanation: Hydrographic surveying encompasses surveys of water bodies (oceans, lakes, rivers, harbors) for navigation, bathymetry, and shorelines.

questions.question: Offsets are said to be large when offset length exceeds _________ m.
questions.explanation: In chain surveying, perpendicular offsets exceeding 15 meters in length are categorized as long offsets (short offsets are ≤ 15 m).

questions.question: A set of arrows provided with chain has _________ arrows.
questions.explanation: A standard set of survey arrows accompanying a metric chain consists of 10 arrows made of tempered 4 mm steel wire.

questions.question: Which of the following instrument is used for ranging ?
questions.explanation: A line ranger is an optical instrument consisting of two 90° reflecting prisms used for fixing intermediate ranging points without an assistant at the ends.

questions.question: The horizontal angle which a line makes with the meridian is called
questions.explanation: The horizontal angle measured between a survey line and a reference meridian (true, magnetic, or arbitrary) is defined as its bearing.

questions.question: The graduated ring being attached to the magnetic needle remains stationary in
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the graduated aluminum ring is attached directly to the broad magnetic needle and remains stationary pointing magnetic North.

questions.question: In a prismatic compass 180° is marked at
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is engraved at the South end and 180° is at the North end so that the bearing can be read directly through the prism at the eye vane.

questions.question: The bearing of a line taken from the starting point of the line towards the direction in which survey progress is called
questions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line taken in the forward direction of progress of the survey from the starting station is called the Fore Bearing (FB).

questions.question: In the whole circle bearing systems, S 85°- 45' W will be expressed as
questions.explanation: S 85°-45' W lies in the 3rd quadrant (SW). WCB = 180° + 85°45' = 265°45'.

questions.question: At poles the magnetic dip is equal to
questions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination of the needle to the horizontal. It is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° (vertical) at the magnetic poles.

questions.question: The whole circle bearing of a line observed by a prismatic compass is 110°, its bearing read on a surveyor's compass is
questions.explanation: A WCB of 110° lies in the 2nd quadrant (SE). Reduced Bearing (QB) = 180° - 110° = S 70° E.

questions.question: The horizontal angle which magnetic meridian makes with the true meridian is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the magnetic meridian and the true (geographical) meridian at a place.

questions.question: The line joining places of equal declination
questions.explanation: Isogonic lines are imaginary lines connecting points on the earth's surface that have the same magnetic declination. (Agonic lines have zero declination).

questions.question: The fore bearing of a line is S 45° 10' E find the back bearing
questions.explanation: To convert Fore Bearing to Back Bearing in Quadrantal system, retain numerical angle and reverse quadrant letters: S 45°10' E becomes N 45°10' W.

questions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is 190° and the magnetic declination is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line
questions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination = 190° - 2° (West declination is subtracted) = 188°.

questions.question: The permissible error in prismatic compass survey is
questions.explanation: In prismatic compass surveying, the permissible error of closure is generally specified as 1 in 340 (or an angular limit of 20').

questions.question: Meridian joining earth's true north and south is called
questions.explanation: The true meridian is the imaginary great circle passing through the geographical north and south poles of the earth and the observer's position.

questions.question: Convert Q.B., S 45° 00' E into W.C.B.
questions.explanation: S 45° 00' E lies in the second quadrant (SE). WCB = 180° - 45°00' = 135° 00'.

questions.question: W.C.B. of a survey line is determined using
questions.explanation: A prismatic compass reads Whole Circle Bearings (0° to 360°) directly through its viewing prism.

questions.question: Theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed irregular hexagon is:
questions.explanation: The theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed polygon with n sides is (2n - 4) × 90°. For a hexagon (n = 6): (12 - 4) × 90° = 720°.

questions.question: Convert W.C.B. 320° 00' into Q.B.
questions.explanation: A WCB of 320° 00' lies in the 4th quadrant (NW). Reduced Bearing = 360° - 320°00' = N 40° 00' W.

questions.question: 0° is engraved at ___________ of the graduated ring of the prismatic compass.
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is graduated at the South end of the ring because reading is done through the prism at the diametrically opposite side.

questions.question: W.C.B. is always reckoned from
questions.explanation: Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) is always measured clockwise starting from the magnetic or true North direction.

questions.question: Magnetic bearing of a line determined was 140° but later it was found that Declination at the place is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line.
questions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination. Here Magnetic Bearing = 140°, Declination = 2° W. True Bearing = 140° - 2° = 138°.

questions.question: Change in declination at place happening in 24 hours is type of variation.
questions.explanation: Diurnal variation is the daily cyclic oscillation of the magnetic needle caused by the rotation of the earth and solar radiation over 24 hours.

questions.question: F.B. of RS is S 45° 15' E. F.B. of PR is S 30° 00' E. Included angle PRS measured in clockwise direction is:
questions.explanation: Included angle at station R: Computed from the back bearing of PR and forward bearing of RS; measured clockwise as 164° 45'.

questions.question: Magnetic equator is an example for
questions.explanation: The magnetic equator is an aclinic line where the magnetic dip is zero (the magnetic needle remains horizontal).

questions.question: F.B. of CD is 30°. FB of DE is 260°. Find ∠CDE measured in clockwise direction:
questions.explanation: Deflection angle / included angle between CD (FB = 30°) and DE (FB = 260°): Clockwise angle ∠CDE = 50°.

questions.question: Bearing measured in the direction of the progress of surveying is called
questions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line measured in the direction of the forward progress of the survey is the Fore Bearing (FB).

questions.question: F.B. of a line PQ is 140°. What is the F.B. of the line QP ?
questions.explanation: If Fore Bearing of PQ = 140°, the Fore Bearing of QP is its Back Bearing: BB = 140° + 180° = 320°.

questions.question: Vertical angle with which magnetic needle makes with the horizontal is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination that a freely suspended magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane.

questions.question: Which method of plane table survey is also used for plotting the distant and inaccessible objects, broken boundaries, river etc?
questions.explanation: The intersection method in plane tabling is ideal for mapping distant, inaccessible points, river boundaries, and broken ground without measuring distances on ground.

questions.question: The process of putting the positions occupied by the board at various survey stations are kept parallel is known as
questions.explanation: Orientation is the process of keeping the plane table at each successive station parallel to the position it occupied at the first station.

questions.question: What is the name of method used in plane table survey similar to that of compass survey?
questions.explanation: Plane table traversing is similar to compass traversing, running a connected series of lines from station to station.

questions.question: Which type of survey cannot be done in dense wooded areas?
questions.explanation: Plane table surveying requires unobstructed sight lines and daylight; it cannot be effectively conducted in dense wooded forests or wet rainy climates.

questions.question: The three points problem may be solved by
questions.explanation: The three-point problem in plane tabling can be solved by mechanical (tracing paper), graphical (Bessel's / cutting arcs), and trial & error (Lehmann's) methods.

questions.question: Instrument used for sighting objects and drawing rays in plane tabling is
questions.explanation: An alidade (plain or telescopic) is the primary sighting and ray-drawing instrument used in plane table surveying.

questions.question: ___________ surveying can be performed without field book.
questions.explanation: In plane table surveying, observations and plotting are performed concurrently in the field on the drawing board, eliminating the need for a field notebook.

questions.question: Which of the following plane table method involves in finding an instrument station ?
questions.explanation: Resection is the plane table method where the position of an unknown occupied instrument station is located on the drawing board by sighting known visible stations.

questions.question: Bessel's solution to three point problem is related to
questions.explanation: Bessel's method of inscribed circles is an exact graphical solution to the three-point problem in plane tabling.

questions.question: Principle of plane table surveying is
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle of plane table surveying is orientation by parallelism, keeping the table board parallel to its orientation at preceding stations.

questions.question: What is the term that is normal to plumb line at all points?
questions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface that is concentric with the mean spheroidal shape of the earth and perpendicular (normal) to the gravity plumb line at every point.

questions.question: What is the benchmarks established between the G.T.S. benchmarks by the state PWD is known as
questions.explanation: Permanent benchmarks are fixed, durable reference points established by government departments (PWD, Railways) between primary G.T.S. benchmarks.

questions.question: Which level is used for precise levelling work?
questions.explanation: A tilting level allows the telescope with its bubble tube to be tilted slightly in the vertical plane using a micrometer screw, making it suitable for precise levelling.

questions.question: In which staff consist of three parts and one slides into another?
questions.explanation: A Sopwith telescopic staff consists of three sliding telescopic lengths made of seasoned wood or aluminum, extending up to 4 or 5 meters.

questions.question: What is the smallest graduated division in levelling staff?
questions.explanation: The smallest graduation mark on a standard metric levelling staff is 5 mm (0.005 m).

questions.question: Which method of contour is suitable for small and undulating area?
questions.explanation: The square (grid) method is ideal for contouring small, undulating, and moderately flat building sites.

questions.question: Which method is not included in the interpolation of contours?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectioning is a field method used to collect elevation data, not an interpolation technique. Contour interpolation is performed by estimation, arithmetic calculation, or graphical methods.

questions.question: Combined correction for curvature and refraction is
questions.explanation: Combined correction for earth curvature and atmospheric refraction is C_comb = C_c - C_r = 0.0785 D² - 0.0112 D² = 0.0673 D² meters (where D is in km).

questions.question: What is the name of the staff 3m long and the band fitted is graduated in mm used for percise levelling?
questions.explanation: An invar levelling staff has an invar alloy ribbon fitted with millimeter graduations under spring tension, ensuring minimal thermal expansion for precise levelling.

questions.question: What R.F. is select for drawing town planning schemes, reservoirs etc?
questions.explanation: For reservoir surveys, town planning, and catchment mapping, small to intermediate representative fractions such as 1/5000 (or 1/2500) are standard.

questions.question: Contour lines of different elevations can unite to form one line in ______
questions.explanation: Contour lines of different elevations coalesce into a single line along a vertical cliff (and cross each other only in an overhanging cliff or cave).

questions.question: The method of indirect levelling in which the relative elevations of different points are obtained by measuring the vertical angles and horizontal distance is known as
questions.explanation: Trigonometrical levelling is an indirect method where the relative difference in elevation is computed from measured vertical angles and horizontal distances.

questions.question: What benchmark is established for short duration such as at the end of a day's work?
questions.explanation: A temporary benchmark (TBM) is established at the close of a day's work on a permanent object (culvert, rock) so that levelling can resume the next day.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to establishing grade contour?
questions.explanation: An Abney level is a hand-held clinometer/level used for measuring ground slope and setting out grade contours in road reconnaissance.

questions.question: Which is prismoidal formula for volume?
questions.explanation: The Prismoidal formula for volume between three equidistant parallel cross-sections of spacing L is V = (L / 6) × [A1 + 4A2 + A3].

questions.question: Boundary of a catchment area will be
questions.explanation: The natural boundary of a catchment/watershed basin separating drainage basins is the ridge line (watershed divide).

questions.question: Which of the following level's telescope can be rotated by surveyor in vertical plane in a smaller amount ?
questions.explanation: A tilting level possesses a micrometer tilting screw that tilts the telescope slightly in the vertical plane to level the line of sight precisely.

questions.question: Station where which B.S. and F.S. are taken is called
questions.explanation: A change point (turning point) is a temporary staff station on which both a Fore Sight (FS) and Back Sight (BS) are taken to transfer the line of collimation.

questions.question: Contour lines merge in the case of
questions.explanation: Contour lines merge together into a single line at a vertical cliff, where points of different elevations share the exact same horizontal coordinate.

questions.question: Following observations were done in reciprocal leveling. Find level difference between A and B: Dumpy level at A: staff reading at A = 1.000 m, staff reading at B = 2.500 m. Dumpy level at B: staff reading at A = 1.300 m, staff reading at B = 2.700 m.
questions.explanation: True level difference by reciprocal levelling: h = [(Staff_B1 - Staff_A1) + (Staff_B2 - Staff_A2)] / 2 = [(2.500 - 1.000) + (2.700 - 1.300)] / 2 = [1.500 + 1.400] / 2 = 1.450 m.

questions.question: Gradient existing between two points is found to be 1 in 1000. Level difference between same points is 5.00 m. Find distance between two points:
questions.explanation: Gradient = Fall / Distance => 1/1000 = 5.00 m / Distance => Distance = 5.00 × 1000 = 5000 m = 5 km.

questions.question: In levelling operation, the point of known elevation is termed as
questions.explanation: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent, well-defined point of known elevation above a chosen reference datum.

questions.question: Last level reading taken before shifting a level is entered as
questions.explanation: Fore Sight (FS) is the last staff reading taken in a levelling setup before moving or shifting the instrument.

questions.question: RL of BM is 100.000. Without taking reading on BM another two staff readings, 1.000 and 3.000 were observed. What is the level difference between these two points ?
questions.explanation: Level difference = Difference between staff readings taken from the same instrument setup = 3.000 m - 1.000 m = 2.000 m.

questions.question: Imaginary line formed by joining points of equal elevations on earth's surface is called
questions.explanation: A contour line is an imaginary line on the ground connecting points having the same elevation above a datum surface.

questions.question: Closely spaced contours indicate
questions.explanation: When contour lines are closely spaced together, they indicate a steep slope; widely spaced contours indicate a gentle or flat slope.

mockTests.title: Basic Engineering Drawing 50 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Comprehensive 50-question Kerala PSC examination covering Basic Engineering Drawing: Drawing sheet sizes & layout (IS 10711, A0-A5, ratio 1:2 and √2:1, folding rules), Drafting instruments (T-square T0-T3, protractor, pencil grades H/2H/HB), Lines & Lettering (IS 10714 line types A-F, IS 9609 lettering height, long/short break lines), Scales (RF, reducing/enlarging, plain, diagonal LC 0.01mm, retrograde/backward vernier), Geometrical construction & Conics (ellipse e<1, parabola e=1, hyperbola e>1 & asymptotes, cutting planes), Dimensioning systems (unidirectional vs aligned, spacing, leader lines, sphere Sϕ50), and Projections (1st vs 3rd angle, projection of points and straight lines, isometric scale 0.816). Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority / PWD

questions.question: The areas of the two subsequent sizes of drawing papers are in the ratio:
questions.explanation: According to standard paper sizing (ISO / BIS), each subsequent smaller size is obtained by halving the larger size along its longer dimension (A_{n+1} = 1/2 A_n). Thus, the ratio of areas of two consecutive sheet sizes is 1 : 2.
questions.rankerTip: Area ratio of consecutive sheet sizes (e.g., A1 to A0) is 1:2. Length to width aspect ratio of any single standard sheet is √2 : 1 (1.414 : 1).

questions.question: What is the length to width ratio of the A2 drawing paper?
questions.explanation: All standard trimmed paper sheets (A0 through A5) maintain a constant aspect ratio of length : width = √2 : 1 ≈ 1.414 : 1 (for A2: 594 mm × 420 mm, where 594 / 420 ≈ √2).
questions.rankerTip: Length : Width ratio for all standard "A" series sheets is √2 : 1 ≈ 1.414 : 1.

questions.question: A diagonal scale of RF 10 is constructed to measure maximum distance of 10 mm. The LC (Least Count) of this scale would be:
questions.explanation: A diagonal scale is used to measure three units or two decimal fractions. When measuring up to millimetres, the diagonal divisions divide the sub-unit (0.1 mm) into 10 parts, giving a least count of 0.01 mm.
questions.rankerTip: Least count of diagonal scale measuring down to 2 decimal places in mm is 0.01 mm.

questions.question: Scale used in a drawing is 1:2. The actual length of a 10 mm line in the drawing is:
questions.explanation: Representative Fraction (RF) = Drawing Length / Actual Length ⇒ 1/2 = 10 mm / Actual Length ⇒ Actual Length = 10 × 2 = 20 mm.
questions.rankerTip: RF = 1:2 is a reducing scale. Actual Length = Drawing Length / RF = 10 / (1/2) = 20 mm.

questions.question: Which of the following is Hyperbola Equation?
questions.explanation: The standard Cartesian equation of a hyperbola centered at the origin is x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 (eccentricity e > 1). x² = 4ay is a parabola, and x² + y² = 1 is a circle.
questions.rankerTip: Ellipse: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (e < 1); Hyperbola: x²/a² - y²/b² = 1 (e > 1); Parabola: y² = 4ax (e = 1); Circle: x² + y² = r² (e = 0).

questions.question: Instrument used to measure angles or drawing lines at the given angles is called as:
questions.explanation: A protractor is a semicircular or circular drafting tool graduated in degrees from 0° to 180° (or 360°) specifically designed to measure and plot angles.
questions.rankerTip: Protractor measures and sets angles. Compass draws circles and arcs. Divider transfers dimensions.

questions.question: A four-sided figure with its opposite sides equal but the angles are not right angles is known as:
questions.explanation: A rhomboid is a parallelogram in which opposite sides are parallel and equal, but adjacent sides are unequal and interior angles are oblique (not 90°). In a rhombus, all four sides are equal.
questions.rankerTip: Opposite sides equal & angles not 90° = Rhomboid. All 4 sides equal & angles not 90° = Rhombus.

questions.question: Dimensioning starting from a common feature and shown to the right and to the left of the common feature is called:
questions.explanation: Superimposed running dimensioning originating from a common zero/datum point in two opposite directions is classified under parallel dimensioning.
questions.rankerTip: Parallel dimensioning uses a common baseline or datum feature. Chain dimensioning places dimensions in continuous series end-to-end.

questions.question: In unidirectional system the dimensions are:
options: Placed by breaking the dimension line in middle
questions.explanation: In unidirectional dimensioning, all dimensional values are aligned horizontally and placed within an interruption (break) in the middle of the dimension line so that they can be read solely from the bottom of the drawing sheet.
questions.rankerTip: Unidirectional system: dimensions are horizontal, breaking the dimension line, read only from bottom. Aligned system: placed above and parallel to dimension line, read from bottom and right.

questions.question: Which grade of pencil is used for drawing arrowheads?
questions.explanation: Arrowheads, lettering, dimensions, and finished visible outlines are drawn with an H pencil (sharp and dense black lines without smudging). 2H/3H pencils are used for construction and projection lines.
questions.rankerTip: H pencil is standard for arrowheads, dimensions, lettering, and outlines. 2H is for construction and dimension lines.

questions.question: Which is the standard code specifies the sizes and layout of drawing sheet?
questions.explanation: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) IS 10711-1983 (SP 46) specifies the sizes and layout of drawing sheets. (IS 9609 is for lettering, IS 10714 is for general line conventions).
questions.rankerTip: IS 10711 = Sizes and layout of drawing sheets; IS 9609 = Lettering; IS 10714 = Lines; IS 11669 = Dimensioning.

questions.question: The distance of the top view of a point A situated 20 mm below HP and 30 mm behind VP is:
questions.explanation: The point is in the 3rd quadrant (below HP, behind VP). When the horizontal plane is rotated 90° clockwise into the vertical plane, the portion behind VP rotates above the reference XY line. Thus, the top view lies 30 mm above the XY line, while the front view lies 20 mm below the XY line.
questions.rankerTip: 3rd quadrant: Top view is above XY line by distance behind VP (30 mm); Front view is below XY line by distance below HP (20 mm).

questions.question: Which diagram below shows a correct geometrical construction of bisecting an angle?
options: Arc centered on angle arm only
Bisector perpendicular to base without intersection
Single arc with non-intersecting radial lines
Arc intersecting both arms, intersecting arcs drawn from these points, and line from vertex passing through the intersection
questions.explanation: To bisect an angle, draw an arc of arbitrary radius centered at vertex O cutting arms at A and B. Then, from centers A and B, draw arcs of equal radius intersecting at point P. The ray OP is the true angle bisector.
questions.rankerTip: Angle bisector construction: center at vertex cuts both arms, then equal intersecting arcs from those arm points form the bisector ray.

questions.question: When the cutting plane is inclined to the axis of the right circular cone and parallel to one of its generators, the section obtained is:
questions.explanation: If a cutting plane cuts through a cone parallel to any one generator (i.e., angle of cutting plane θ = α, the semi-vertical angle), the resulting conic section is a parabola.
questions.rankerTip: Parallel to generator (θ = α) = Parabola; Cuts all generators (θ > α) = Ellipse; Parallel to axis (θ < α) = Hyperbola; Perpendicular to axis = Circle.

questions.question: Which of the following conics has an eccentricity as unity?
questions.explanation: Eccentricity (e) values: Circle: e = 0; Ellipse: 0 < e < 1; Parabola: e = 1 (unity); Hyperbola: e > 1.
questions.rankerTip: Circle: e = 0; Ellipse: e < 1; Parabola: e = 1; Hyperbola: e > 1.

questions.question: How many pairs of parallel lines are there in regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has 6 equal edges forming 3 pairs of mutually parallel opposite sides.
questions.rankerTip: Regular hexagon has 6 sides, opposite sides are parallel, yielding 6 / 2 = 3 pairs of parallel lines.

questions.question: Standard size of drawing sheets recommended by the Bureau of Indian Standards is:
questions.explanation: These are the trimmed sizes for standard drawing sheets specified by BIS (IS 10711): A4 (210 × 297 mm), A3 (297 × 420 mm), and A2 (420 × 594 mm).

questions.question: Which of the following pencil leads is hardest?
questions.explanation: The pencil hardness scale from soft to hard is: 7B ... B < HB < F < H ... 9H. Among HB, H, B, and F, H has the highest lead hardness.
questions.rankerTip: Order of increasing hardness: 7B to B < HB < F < H to 9H. Hardest among (HB, H, B, F) is H.

questions.question: When 1 cm on a map represents 10 m on the ground, representative fraction is:
questions.explanation: RF = Drawing length / Actual length = 1 cm / 10 m = 1 cm / (10 × 100 cm) = 1 / 1000.

questions.question: In the first angle projection:
options: Object is between the observer and the plane of projection
Plane of projection is between the observer and the object
questions.explanation: In 1st angle projection, the object lies in quadrant I: Observer → Object → Projection Plane. In 3rd angle projection, the projection plane lies between the observer and the object.
questions.rankerTip: 1st angle: Observer -> Object -> Plane. 3rd angle: Observer -> Plane -> Object.

questions.question: The dotted line (dashed line) represents:
questions.explanation: Dashed lines of medium thickness (Type E / Type F according to IS 10714) represent hidden outlines and hidden edges in engineering views.
questions.rankerTip: Dashed lines (medium thickness) = hidden edges. Thin continuous = dimension/projection lines. Thin chain = center lines.

questions.question: The ratio of isometric length to its true length is nearly:
questions.explanation: Isometric Length / True Length = √(2/3) = cos 45° / cos 30° ≈ 0.8165 (or 81.65%).
questions.rankerTip: Isometric length = 0.816 × True length (or √(2/3) × True length).

questions.question: Scale representing three different units such as metre, decimetre and centimetre is:
questions.explanation: A diagonal scale can read up to three successive units (e.g., yards, feet, and inches, or metres, decimetres, and centimetres) or up to two decimal places.
questions.rankerTip: Plain scale = 2 units. Diagonal scale = 3 units. Vernier scale = fractional parts of smallest division.

questions.question: The size of the letter is described by its:
questions.explanation: According to BIS IS 9609, standard lettering size (h) is always designated by the nominal height of capital letters in millimetres (2.5, 3.5, 5, 7, 10, 14, 20 mm).
questions.rankerTip: Nominal height (h) of capital letters defines the lettering size as per IS 9609.

questions.question: The scale on which three dimensions can be measured is known as:
questions.explanation: Measuring three dimensions or up to two decimal places is done using a diagonal scale based on the principle of similar triangles.
questions.rankerTip: Diagonal scale measures 3 dimensions/units based on similar triangles.

questions.question: The drawing sheet is so folded that the ------- is always on the top:
questions.explanation: Standard folding rules (IS 10711) mandate that the title block (at the bottom-right corner of the sheet) must remain completely visible on the top front fold for quick identification in filing.
questions.rankerTip: Title block must always appear on the top fold of folded drawings (IS 10711).

questions.question: Outline or principal lines are drawn as:
questions.explanation: Visible outlines, edges, and principal boundaries are designated as Type A lines (Continuous thick lines, approximately 0.5 mm to 0.7 mm).
questions.rankerTip: Type A line = Continuous thick = Visible outlines and principal edges.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symbol of the first angle projection?
options: Truncated cone with smaller base on left, followed by concentric circles on right
Concentric circles on left, followed by truncated cone on right
questions.explanation: In 1st angle projection, the right-side view is projected onto the left plane or viewed from the left and projected to the right. The standard ISO/BIS symbol shows the frustum on the left and the circular views on the right.
questions.rankerTip: 1st Angle symbol: frustum on left, concentric circles on right. 3rd Angle symbol: concentric circles on left, frustum on right.

questions.question: Line AB 30° inclined to HP and parallel to VP. If the line is at first quadrant which one of the following statement is correct?
options: Elevation will be of actual length 30° inclined and below XY line
Elevation will be shorter than actual length and above XY line
Elevation will be shorter than actual length 30° inclined and below XY line
Elevation will be of actual length 30° inclined and above XY line
questions.explanation: In the 1st quadrant, elevation (front view) appears above the XY line. Because the line is parallel to VP, its projection on VP shows its true/actual length and true inclination of 30° to HP.
questions.rankerTip: Line parallel to VP: front view (elevation) shows true length and true inclination θ to HP, situated above XY in 1st quadrant.

questions.question: The outer line of an objects are drawn using ------- Pencil.
questions.explanation: An H pencil is standard for visible outlines, border finishing, and dimensioning arrowheads in professional drafting.
questions.rankerTip: Outlines & border lines = H pencil; Construction lines = 2H/3H; Freehand sketching/lettering = HB/H.

questions.question: Which one of the following statement is not correct in the case of aligned system?
options: Dimension value placed perpendicular to the dimension line
Dimension can be read only from the bottom edge of the drawing sheet
Dimension can be read from the bottom edge or right hand edge of the drawing sheet
Dimension should be placed near the middle and above but clear of the dimension line
questions.explanation: In an aligned system, dimensions are aligned parallel to the dimension lines and read from the bottom or the right-hand edge. Reading only from the bottom edge describes the unidirectional system, not the aligned system.
questions.rankerTip: Aligned system allows reading from bottom and right-hand edge. Unidirectional allows reading only from bottom.

questions.question: The first dimension line should be placed at least:
questions.explanation: Drafting standards recommend placing the first dimension line at least 10 mm away from the outline of the object, with parallel dimension lines spaced at least 6 to 8 mm apart.
questions.rankerTip: First dimension line: minimum 10 mm from outline. Successive parallel dimension lines: minimum 6 to 8 mm apart.

questions.question: A line CD 141.4 mm long inclined 45° to vertical plane and parallel to horizontal plane. The front view of line CD measures ...... mm:
questions.rankerTip: Front view of line inclined to VP by ϕ: Length = L cos ϕ = 141.4 × cos 45° = 100 mm.

questions.question: If a line is inclined at 45° to the HP and 30° to the VP, its front view is inclined at:
questions.explanation: The apparent angle of elevation α satisfies tan α = tan θ / cos ϕ. With θ = 45° and ϕ = 30°: tan α = tan 45° / cos 30° = 1 / 0.8660 ≈ 1.1547 > 1, so α > 45° (specifically α ≈ 49.1°).
questions.rankerTip: Apparent inclination α is always GREATER than true inclination θ to HP (tan α = tan θ / cos ϕ).

questions.question: Which one of the following scales is the smallest?
questions.explanation: Comparing Representative Fractions: (a) 1 mm / 1 m = 1/1000; (b) RF = 1/2000; (c) RF = 1/20000; (d) 1 cm / 1 km = 1 / 100,000. 1/100,000 is the smallest fraction, so (d) is the smallest scale.
questions.rankerTip: 1 cm = 1 km means RF = 1 / 100,000, which has the largest denominator and is thus the smallest scale.

questions.question: The T-Square with the working edge length of 1000 ± 10 mm, is designated as:
questions.explanation: Standard T-square sizes according to BIS (IS 1364): T0: 1500 mm; T1: 1000 mm; T2: 700 mm; T3: 500 mm.
questions.rankerTip: T-Square designations: T0 (1500 mm), T1 (1000 mm), T2 (700 mm), T3 (500 mm).

questions.question: An ellipse has ------- vertices and ------- foci.
questions.explanation: An ellipse has two principal vertices (the endpoints of the major axis) and two foci (F1 and F2).
questions.rankerTip: Ellipse has 2 vertices and 2 foci. Parabola has 1 vertex and 1 focus. Hyperbola has 2 vertices and 2 foci.

questions.question: 10 centimetre is:
questions.explanation: In metric measurement: 10 mm = 1 cm; 10 cm = 1 decimetre (dm); 10 dm = 1 metre (m).
questions.rankerTip: 10 mm = 1 cm; 10 cm = 1 decimetre (dm); 100 cm = 1 metre.

questions.question: "Asymptote" is:
options: Tangents drawn from infinity to a circle
Tangents drawn from infinity to a hyperbola
questions.explanation: An asymptote is a straight line that a curve approaches arbitrarily closely as it heads toward infinity; for a hyperbola, asymptotes are tangents to the curve at infinity passing through the center.
questions.rankerTip: Asymptotes are tangents to the hyperbola at infinity, intersecting at the center of the hyperbola.

questions.question: Where the plan is placed in third angle projection?
