bankQuestions.question: The correction for sag is always _____
bankQuestions.explanation: Correction for sag is always negative (-ve) because the catenary curve makes the measured distance between supports longer than the true straight chord distance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sag correction is ALWAYS negative (-ve).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q16) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: If L is the correct length of a chain, L' is the incorrect length and D' is the measured length, then the correct length is:
bankQuestions.explanation: True distance = (Measured length) × (Incorrect length of chain / True length of chain) = D' × (L' / L).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True × True = Wrong × Wrong => True Distance = (L'/L) × D'.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q17) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The instrument which is not used in chain survey is
bankQuestions.explanation: A levelling staff is used exclusively in levelling and tachometric work to measure vertical elevations, not for linear distance measurement in chain surveying.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Levelling staff is for vertical measurements, not chain surveying.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q18) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The Principle of chain surveying is
bankQuestions.explanation: The fundamental principle of chain surveying is triangulation, whereby the survey area is partitioned into a network of well-conditioned triangles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chain survey principle: Triangulation.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q19) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The system of lines or Triangles covering the area to be surveyed is
bankQuestions.explanation: The system of survey lines forming the skeleton network of triangles covering the area to be surveyed is called the framework.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Framework: network of survey lines covering the ground.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q20) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: In a well-conditioned triangle the angles are
bankQuestions.explanation: A well-conditioned triangle has no angle less than 30° and no angle greater than 120° to minimize geometric plotting distortion.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Angles between 30° and 120°. Ideal triangle is equilateral (60°).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q21) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The line joining some fixed points termed as tie stations on main survey line is called
bankQuestions.explanation: A tie line joins auxiliary (tie) stations on main survey lines to measure offsets for locating interior ground details.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tie line: locates interior details and avoids long offsets.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q22) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Invar tape is made up of an alloy of and steel.
bankQuestions.explanation: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy (36% Nickel, 64% Steel) characterized by an exceptionally low coefficient of thermal expansion.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Invar = 36% Nickel + 64% Steel.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q21) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The process of establishing an intermediate point in a line is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Ranging is the operational process of aligning intermediate points along a straight survey line between two terminal stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Establishing points in a straight line = Ranging.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q26) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Error =
options: Difference in values and sign of observed value
Difference in values and sign of true value
bankQuestions.explanation: By standard definition, Error = Observed Value - True Value (while Correction = True Value - Observed Value = -Error).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Error = Observed - True. Correction = True - Observed.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q28) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Of the following, which is the primary stage of surveying ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Reconnaissance is the initial ground inspection of the survey area to observe boundaries, terrain features, and select station points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First stage of any survey is Reconnaissance (Recce).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q31) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Bad ranging is an example for
bankQuestions.explanation: Bad (imperfect) ranging causes the chain to deviate from a true straight line, consistently making the measured length greater than the true length (positive cumulative error).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bad ranging is ALWAYS a positive cumulative error (+ve error, requires -ve correction).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q32) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Survey lines set out to locate interior details of a plot is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Tie lines are secondary lines run across main survey lines to locate interior ground features and details.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tie lines locate interior details; check lines check accuracy.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q33) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: A link of a metric chain is cm in length.
bankQuestions.explanation: Each link of a standard 20 m or 30 m metric chain measures 0.2 m (20 cm) between the centers of connecting rings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metric chain link = 20 cm = 0.2 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q35) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is the prime instrument is used for ranging ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Ranging rods (typically 2 to 3 m long, octagonal or circular poles painted in alternating red/black and white bands) are the prime tools for visual alignment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ranging rod is the primary ranging instrument.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q37) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: A 20 m metric chain has links.
bankQuestions.explanation: A 20-meter metric chain consists of 100 links (each link = 20 cm = 0.2 m). A 30 m metric chain has 150 links.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 20 m = 100 links; 30 m = 150 links.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q39) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: 90° is set out using:
bankQuestions.explanation: An open cross-staff is used on survey lines to set out right angles (90°) for perpendicular offsets.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open cross-staff: 90°; French cross-staff: 45° and 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q40) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: ___________ angles can be set out using French cross staff.
bankQuestions.explanation: An octagonal French cross staff has sighting slits set at angles that allow setting out both 45° and 90° lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: French cross-staff sets out 45° and 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q41) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Gunter's chain is ___________ in length.
bankQuestions.explanation: Gunter's chain (surveyor's chain) is 66 feet long and contains 100 links (1 link = 0.66 ft = 7.92 in).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q42) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Survey related to large water bodies is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Hydrographic surveying encompasses surveys of water bodies (oceans, lakes, rivers, harbors) for navigation, bathymetry, and shorelines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Survey of water bodies = Hydrographic surveying.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q74) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Offsets are said to be large when offset length exceeds _________ m.
bankQuestions.explanation: In chain surveying, perpendicular offsets exceeding 15 meters in length are categorized as long offsets (short offsets are ≤ 15 m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Short offsets ≤ 15 m; Long offsets > 15 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q87) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: A set of arrows provided with chain has _________ arrows.
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard set of survey arrows accompanying a metric chain consists of 10 arrows made of tempered 4 mm steel wire.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 10 arrows accompany each chain.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q88) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following instrument is used for ranging ?
bankQuestions.explanation: A line ranger is an optical instrument consisting of two 90° reflecting prisms used for fixing intermediate ranging points without an assistant at the ends.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line ranger allows a single surveyor to fix intermediate points.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q91) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The horizontal angle which a line makes with the meridian is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The horizontal angle measured between a survey line and a reference meridian (true, magnetic, or arbitrary) is defined as its bearing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Angle with meridian = Bearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q23) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The graduated ring being attached to the magnetic needle remains stationary in
bankQuestions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the graduated aluminum ring is attached directly to the broad magnetic needle and remains stationary pointing magnetic North.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismatic: ring attached to needle, remains stationary. Surveyor: ring fixed to box.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q24) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: In a prismatic compass 180° is marked at
bankQuestions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is engraved at the South end and 180° is at the North end so that the bearing can be read directly through the prism at the eye vane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 0° at South, 180° at North, 90° at West, 270° at East.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q25) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The bearing of a line taken from the starting point of the line towards the direction in which survey progress is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line taken in the forward direction of progress of the survey from the starting station is called the Fore Bearing (FB).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In direction of survey = Fore bearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q26) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: In the whole circle bearing systems, S 85°- 45' W will be expressed as
bankQuestions.explanation: S 85°-45' W lies in the 3rd quadrant (SW). WCB = 180° + 85°45' = 265°45'.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q27) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: At poles the magnetic dip is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination of the needle to the horizontal. It is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° (vertical) at the magnetic poles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dip at Equator = 0°; Dip at Poles = 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q28) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The whole circle bearing of a line observed by a prismatic compass is 110°, its bearing read on a surveyor's compass is
bankQuestions.explanation: A WCB of 110° lies in the 2nd quadrant (SE). Reduced Bearing (QB) = 180° - 110° = S 70° E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 110° in SE quadrant: 180° - 110° = S 70° E.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q29) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The horizontal angle which magnetic meridian makes with the true meridian is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the magnetic meridian and the true (geographical) meridian at a place.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal angle = Magnetic Declination. Vertical angle = Dip.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q30) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The line joining places of equal declination
bankQuestions.explanation: Isogonic lines are imaginary lines connecting points on the earth's surface that have the same magnetic declination. (Agonic lines have zero declination).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal declination = Isogonic. Zero declination = Agonic.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q31) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The fore bearing of a line is S 45° 10' E find the back bearing
bankQuestions.explanation: To convert Fore Bearing to Back Bearing in Quadrantal system, retain numerical angle and reverse quadrant letters: S 45°10' E becomes N 45°10' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: S becomes N, E becomes W: N 45° 10' W.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q32) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is 190° and the magnetic declination is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination = 190° - 2° (West declination is subtracted) = 188°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TB = MB + East Declination / TB = MB - West Declination = 190° - 2° = 188°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q33) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The permissible error in prismatic compass survey is
bankQuestions.explanation: In prismatic compass surveying, the permissible error of closure is generally specified as 1 in 340 (or an angular limit of 20').
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 in 340 (or 20 minutes) is standard permissible compass error.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q34) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Meridian joining earth's true north and south is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The true meridian is the imaginary great circle passing through the geographical north and south poles of the earth and the observer's position.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Through true geographic poles = True meridian.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q27) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Convert Q.B., S 45° 00' E into W.C.B.
bankQuestions.explanation: S 45° 00' E lies in the second quadrant (SE). WCB = 180° - 45°00' = 135° 00'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SE quadrant: WCB = 180° - 45° = 135°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q43) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: W.C.B. of a survey line is determined using
bankQuestions.explanation: A prismatic compass reads Whole Circle Bearings (0° to 360°) directly through its viewing prism.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismatic compass = Whole Circle Bearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q45) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed irregular hexagon is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed polygon with n sides is (2n - 4) × 90°. For a hexagon (n = 6): (12 - 4) × 90° = 720°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90° = 8 × 90° = 720°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q47) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Convert W.C.B. 320° 00' into Q.B.
bankQuestions.explanation: A WCB of 320° 00' lies in the 4th quadrant (NW). Reduced Bearing = 360° - 320°00' = N 40° 00' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 4th quadrant (NW): 360° - 320° = N 40° W.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q49) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: 0° is engraved at ___________ of the graduated ring of the prismatic compass.
bankQuestions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is graduated at the South end of the ring because reading is done through the prism at the diametrically opposite side.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 0° at South, 180° at North.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q50) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: W.C.B. is always reckoned from
bankQuestions.explanation: Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) is always measured clockwise starting from the magnetic or true North direction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: WCB is always measured clockwise from North (0° to 360°).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q52) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Magnetic bearing of a line determined was 140° but later it was found that Declination at the place is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line.
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination. Here Magnetic Bearing = 140°, Declination = 2° W. True Bearing = 140° - 2° = 138°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q53) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Change in declination at place happening in 24 hours is type of variation.
bankQuestions.explanation: Diurnal variation is the daily cyclic oscillation of the magnetic needle caused by the rotation of the earth and solar radiation over 24 hours.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Daily variation in 24 hours = Diurnal variation.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q56) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: F.B. of RS is S 45° 15' E. F.B. of PR is S 30° 00' E. Included angle PRS measured in clockwise direction is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Included angle at station R: Computed from the back bearing of PR and forward bearing of RS; measured clockwise as 164° 45'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Clockwise angle PRS = 164° 45'.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q60) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Magnetic equator is an example for
bankQuestions.explanation: The magnetic equator is an aclinic line where the magnetic dip is zero (the magnetic needle remains horizontal).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Zero dip = Aclinic line (Magnetic equator). Equal dip = Isoclinic line.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q76) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: F.B. of CD is 30°. FB of DE is 260°. Find ∠CDE measured in clockwise direction:
bankQuestions.explanation: Deflection angle / included angle between CD (FB = 30°) and DE (FB = 260°): Clockwise angle ∠CDE = 50°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Clockwise angle = 50°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q77) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Bearing measured in the direction of the progress of surveying is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line measured in the direction of the forward progress of the survey is the Fore Bearing (FB).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In direction of progress = Fore bearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q79) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: F.B. of a line PQ is 140°. What is the F.B. of the line QP ?
bankQuestions.explanation: If Fore Bearing of PQ = 140°, the Fore Bearing of QP is its Back Bearing: BB = 140° + 180° = 320°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FB of QP = BB of PQ = 140° + 180° = 320°.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q84) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Vertical angle with which magnetic needle makes with the horizontal is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination that a freely suspended magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical angle = Dip. Horizontal angle = Declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q95) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which method of plane table survey is also used for plotting the distant and inaccessible objects, broken boundaries, river etc?
bankQuestions.explanation: The intersection method in plane tabling is ideal for mapping distant, inaccessible points, river boundaries, and broken ground without measuring distances on ground.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inaccessible objects, rivers, mountainous terrain = Intersection method.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q35) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The process of putting the positions occupied by the board at various survey stations are kept parallel is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: Orientation is the process of keeping the plane table at each successive station parallel to the position it occupied at the first station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Keeping table parallel at successive stations = Orientation.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q36) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of method used in plane table survey similar to that of compass survey?
bankQuestions.explanation: Plane table traversing is similar to compass traversing, running a connected series of lines from station to station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Connected series of lines from station to station = Traversing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q37) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which type of survey cannot be done in dense wooded areas?
bankQuestions.explanation: Plane table surveying requires unobstructed sight lines and daylight; it cannot be effectively conducted in dense wooded forests or wet rainy climates.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane tabling cannot be done in dense woods or rainy weather.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q38) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The three points problem may be solved by
bankQuestions.explanation: The three-point problem in plane tabling can be solved by mechanical (tracing paper), graphical (Bessel's / cutting arcs), and trial & error (Lehmann's) methods.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: All three: Tracing paper, Bessel's, and Lehmann's trial & error.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q39) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Instrument used for sighting objects and drawing rays in plane tabling is
bankQuestions.explanation: An alidade (plain or telescopic) is the primary sighting and ray-drawing instrument used in plane table surveying.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Alidade sights objects and draws rays along fiducial edge.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q24) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: ___________ surveying can be performed without field book.
bankQuestions.explanation: In plane table surveying, observations and plotting are performed concurrently in the field on the drawing board, eliminating the need for a field notebook.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table surveying needs no field book because plotting is done on site.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q57) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following plane table method involves in finding an instrument station ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Resection is the plane table method where the position of an unknown occupied instrument station is located on the drawing board by sighting known visible stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Locating instrument station = Resection.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q62) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Bessel's solution to three point problem is related to
bankQuestions.explanation: Bessel's method of inscribed circles is an exact graphical solution to the three-point problem in plane tabling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bessel's method is a Graphical method.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q80) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Principle of plane table surveying is
bankQuestions.explanation: The fundamental principle of plane table surveying is orientation by parallelism, keeping the table board parallel to its orientation at preceding stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parallelism / Orientation.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q81) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: What is the term that is normal to plumb line at all points?
bankQuestions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface that is concentric with the mean spheroidal shape of the earth and perpendicular (normal) to the gravity plumb line at every point.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Normal to plumb line at all points = Level surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q40) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the benchmarks established between the G.T.S. benchmarks by the state PWD is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: Permanent benchmarks are fixed, durable reference points established by government departments (PWD, Railways) between primary G.T.S. benchmarks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Established by State PWD = Permanent benchmark.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q41) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which level is used for precise levelling work?
bankQuestions.explanation: A tilting level allows the telescope with its bubble tube to be tilted slightly in the vertical plane using a micrometer screw, making it suitable for precise levelling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tilting level with micrometer screw is designed for precise levelling.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q42) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: In which staff consist of three parts and one slides into another?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Sopwith telescopic staff consists of three sliding telescopic lengths made of seasoned wood or aluminum, extending up to 4 or 5 meters.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Three parts sliding into one another = Sopwith telescopic staff.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q43) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the smallest graduated division in levelling staff?
bankQuestions.explanation: The smallest graduation mark on a standard metric levelling staff is 5 mm (0.005 m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Least count of metric levelling staff = 5 mm = 0.005 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q44) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which method of contour is suitable for small and undulating area?
bankQuestions.explanation: The square (grid) method is ideal for contouring small, undulating, and moderately flat building sites.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Small and undulating building site = Square (grid) method.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q45) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which method is not included in the interpolation of contours?
bankQuestions.explanation: Cross-sectioning is a field method used to collect elevation data, not an interpolation technique. Contour interpolation is performed by estimation, arithmetic calculation, or graphical methods.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Interpolation methods: Estimation, Arithmetic calculation, and Graphical.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q46) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Combined correction for curvature and refraction is
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction for earth curvature and atmospheric refraction is C_comb = C_c - C_r = 0.0785 D² - 0.0112 D² = 0.0673 D² meters (where D is in km).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C_comb = 0.0673 D² (subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q47) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of the staff 3m long and the band fitted is graduated in mm used for percise levelling?
bankQuestions.explanation: An invar levelling staff has an invar alloy ribbon fitted with millimeter graduations under spring tension, ensuring minimal thermal expansion for precise levelling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 3 m long with invar band graduated in mm = Invar Staff.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q48) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What R.F. is select for drawing town planning schemes, reservoirs etc?
bankQuestions.explanation: For reservoir surveys, town planning, and catchment mapping, small to intermediate representative fractions such as 1/5000 (or 1/2500) are standard.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Town planning & reservoirs: 1/5000.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q49) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines of different elevations can unite to form one line in ______
bankQuestions.explanation: Contour lines of different elevations coalesce into a single line along a vertical cliff (and cross each other only in an overhanging cliff or cave).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Unite into one line = Vertical cliff. Cross each other = Overhanging cliff.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q50) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The method of indirect levelling in which the relative elevations of different points are obtained by measuring the vertical angles and horizontal distance is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: Trigonometrical levelling is an indirect method where the relative difference in elevation is computed from measured vertical angles and horizontal distances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical angles + horizontal distances = Trigonometrical levelling.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q51) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What benchmark is established for short duration such as at the end of a day's work?
bankQuestions.explanation: A temporary benchmark (TBM) is established at the close of a day's work on a permanent object (culvert, rock) so that levelling can resume the next day.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: End of day's work = Temporary benchmark (TBM).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q52) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which instrument is used to establishing grade contour?
bankQuestions.explanation: An Abney level is a hand-held clinometer/level used for measuring ground slope and setting out grade contours in road reconnaissance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Grade contours = Abney level.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q53) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which is prismoidal formula for volume?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Prismoidal formula for volume between three equidistant parallel cross-sections of spacing L is V = (L / 6) × [A1 + 4A2 + A3].
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q54) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Boundary of a catchment area will be
bankQuestions.explanation: The natural boundary of a catchment/watershed basin separating drainage basins is the ridge line (watershed divide).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Catchment boundary = Ridge line / watershed divide.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q23) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following level's telescope can be rotated by surveyor in vertical plane in a smaller amount ?
bankQuestions.explanation: A tilting level possesses a micrometer tilting screw that tilts the telescope slightly in the vertical plane to level the line of sight precisely.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tilting level telescope rotates slightly in vertical plane.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q25) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Station where which B.S. and F.S. are taken is called
bankQuestions.explanation: A change point (turning point) is a temporary staff station on which both a Fore Sight (FS) and Back Sight (BS) are taken to transfer the line of collimation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Both BS and FS taken = Change point (CP).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q44) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines merge in the case of
bankQuestions.explanation: Contour lines merge together into a single line at a vertical cliff, where points of different elevations share the exact same horizontal coordinate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Merge into one line = Vertical cliff.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q46) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Following observations were done in reciprocal leveling. Find level difference between A and B: Dumpy level at A: staff reading at A = 1.000 m, staff reading at B = 2.500 m. Dumpy level at B: staff reading at A = 1.300 m, staff reading at B = 2.700 m.
bankQuestions.explanation: True level difference by reciprocal levelling: h = [(Staff_B1 - Staff_A1) + (Staff_B2 - Staff_A2)] / 2 = [(2.500 - 1.000) + (2.700 - 1.300)] / 2 = [1.500 + 1.400] / 2 = 1.450 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q48) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Gradient existing between two points is found to be 1 in 1000. Level difference between same points is 5.00 m. Find distance between two points:
bankQuestions.explanation: Gradient = Fall / Distance => 1/1000 = 5.00 m / Distance => Distance = 5.00 × 1000 = 5000 m = 5 km.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance = 5 m × 1000 = 5000 m = 5 km.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q61) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: In levelling operation, the point of known elevation is termed as
bankQuestions.explanation: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent, well-defined point of known elevation above a chosen reference datum.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point of known elevation = Bench mark.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q64) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Last level reading taken before shifting a level is entered as
bankQuestions.explanation: Fore Sight (FS) is the last staff reading taken in a levelling setup before moving or shifting the instrument.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Last reading before shifting = Fore Sight (FS).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q66) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: RL of BM is 100.000. Without taking reading on BM another two staff readings, 1.000 and 3.000 were observed. What is the level difference between these two points ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Level difference = Difference between staff readings taken from the same instrument setup = 3.000 m - 1.000 m = 2.000 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Level difference = 3.000 - 1.000 = 2.000 m (independent of BM RL).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q68) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Imaginary line formed by joining points of equal elevations on earth's surface is called
bankQuestions.explanation: A contour line is an imaginary line on the ground connecting points having the same elevation above a datum surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line joining points of equal elevation = Contour.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q69) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Closely spaced contours indicate
bankQuestions.explanation: When contour lines are closely spaced together, they indicate a steep slope; widely spaced contours indicate a gentle or flat slope.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Close contours = Steep slope. Wide contours = Gentle slope.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q75) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: ___________ is the equation for finding correction value for refraction.
bankQuestions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight downward toward the earth, giving a correction of C_r = +0.0112 D² meters (where D is distance in km).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction correction C_r = 0.0112 D² (additive).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q82) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Slope along the longitudinal direction is often termed as
bankQuestions.explanation: The rate of rise or fall of the ground surface along the longitudinal direction of a road, canal, or railway is termed the gradient.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Longitudinal slope = Gradient. Transverse slope = Camber/cross slope.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q83) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Level reading taken on a BM is 2.000. RL of BM is 10.000. Then a level reading of 3.500 was taken on top of a stake. Find the RL of the top of the stake:
bankQuestions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of BM + Staff Reading on BM = 10.000 + 2.000 = 12.000 m. RL of Stake = HI - Reading on Stake = 12.000 - 3.500 = 8.500 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q85) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Equal gradient lines along a slope are called
bankQuestions.explanation: A grade contour is a line on the ground along which a constant uniform slope (gradient) is maintained.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal gradient line = Grade contour.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q86) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The latitude and departure with reference to preceding point are known as _____
bankQuestions.explanation: Consecutive coordinates (latitude and departure) of a station are computed with reference to the immediately preceding traverse station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: With reference to preceding point = Consecutive coordinates.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q55) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the type of angle useful for alignment of highways, railways, canals etc?
bankQuestions.explanation: Deflection angles (angle between prolongation of preceding line and forward line) are extensively used for route surveying of highways, railways, and canals.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Highways, railways, route surveys = Deflection angles.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q56) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the test carried in theodolite to make the horizontal axis perpendicular to the vertical axis?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Spire test (horizontal axis test) is performed to ensure that the horizontal trunnion axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal axis ⊥ Vertical axis = Spire test.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q57) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: When the angular measurements are more precise than the linear measurements, balancing the traverse is done by
bankQuestions.explanation: The Transit rule is applied to adjust traverse misclosure when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch rule: angles and lengths equally precise. Transit rule: angles more precise than lengths.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q58) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The chord between two successive regular stations on a curve is known as _____
bankQuestions.explanation: In curve layout, a normal chord is the full standard chord between two consecutive full chainage peg stations on a circular curve.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Between regular full chainage stations = Normal chord.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q59) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the multiplying constant, if adopting anallatic lens in the telescope of a tacheometer?
bankQuestions.explanation: An anallatic lens placed between the objective and eyepiece eliminates the additive constant (f + d = 0), leaving the multiplying constant k = f/i = 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Anallatic lens: multiplying constant k = 100; additive constant c = 0.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q60) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the distance between point of intersection to point of tangency?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tangent distance is the straight distance measured from the Point of Intersection (V) to either Point of Tangency (T1 or T2): T = R tan(∆/2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Intersection to tangency point = Tangent distance T = R tan(∆/2).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q61) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which curve is generally introduced on highway between a straight and circular curve to provide ease and gradual change of direction?
bankQuestions.explanation: A transition curve (clothoid / spiral) provides a gradual transition from zero curvature on a tangent to the finite radius of a circular curve, preventing sudden centrifugal jerks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Between tangent and circular curve = Transition curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q62) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which method is used for short traverse in theodolite survey?
bankQuestions.explanation: The fast needle method is used for running short traverse lines using the theodolite's compass without individual vernier angle computations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Short traverse = Fast needle method.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q63) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the multiplying constant in tacheometric survey?
bankQuestions.explanation: In tacheometry, the multiplying constant is given by the focal length divided by stadia hair interval: k = f / i (normally designed as 100).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Multiplying constant = f/i. Additive constant = f+d.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q64) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The fine adjustment in theodolite is done by
bankQuestions.explanation: In a theodolite, after clamping the motion screw, fine adjustment and precision sighting of the crosshairs is made using the tangent (slow-motion) screw.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fine motion / precision sighting = Tangent screw.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q81) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The face left position is also called
bankQuestions.explanation: Telescope normal (or face left) describes the position where the vertical circle is situated to the observer's left when looking through the eyepiece.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Face left = Telescope normal. Face right = Telescope reversed / inverted.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q82) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is not a traversing method?
bankQuestions.explanation: Open traversing is a geometric classification of traverse paths (unclosed), whereas chain, compass, theodolite, and plane table traversing are instrument methods.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open/closed are types of traverse, not instrument methods.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q83) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The telescope is rotated in horizontal plane relative to which axis?
bankQuestions.explanation: The telescope of a theodolite rotates in a horizontal plane about its vertical axis. Note: in official PSC provisional key Trunnion axis is given as (C).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trunnion axis (horizontal axis) is official PSC key option C.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q84) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Imaginary line joining centre of the eyepiece and the objective of the telescope is
bankQuestions.explanation: The imaginary line connecting the optical center of the objective lens and the center of the eyepiece is the optical axis of the telescope.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Objective center to eyepiece center = Axis of telescope. Crosshairs to objective center = Line of collimation.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q30) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Horizontal angle as well as vertical angle can be measured using a
bankQuestions.explanation: A transit theodolite is designed to measure both horizontal and vertical angles with high precision.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal and vertical angles = Theodolite.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q34) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Point where the circular curve begins is called as
bankQuestions.explanation: The Point of Curve (P.C.) is the tangent-curve junction where the circular curve begins. Point of Tangency (P.T.) is where it ends.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Begins = P.C. (Point of Curve). Ends = P.T. (Point of Tangency).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q36) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Projection of a survey line onto N-S line is termed as
bankQuestions.explanation: The projection of a traverse survey line onto the North-South reference meridian is called its Latitude (L = l cos θ).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Projection on N-S = Latitude. Projection on E-W = Departure.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q54) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is known as the ideal transition curve ?
bankQuestions.explanation: An ideal transition curve has a rate of change of radial acceleration that is uniform; the clothoid (Euler spiral) meets this condition with curvature increasing linearly with length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ideal transition curve = Clothoid (Euler spiral).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q55) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Process of revolving telescope of theodolite in the horizontal plane with respect to vertical axis of the theodolite is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Swinging the theodolite is the operation of rotating the telescope about the vertical axis in a horizontal plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal plane about vertical axis = Swinging. Vertical plane about horizontal axis = Transiting.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q58) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Angle subtended by radius at the centre of the curve is called as
bankQuestions.explanation: The angle subtended at the center of a circular curve by the arc connecting two tangent points is called the central angle (equal to the total deflection angle ∆).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Angle at the center = Central angle.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q59) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Angle between the preceding line and succeeding line is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The deflection angle is the angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the forward succeeding survey line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Angle between prolongation of line and next line = Deflection angle.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q63) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer fitted with an anallactic lens is
bankQuestions.explanation: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer equipped with an anallatic lens is k = f/i = 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Multiplying constant is 100.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q70) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is called as Easement curve ?
bankQuestions.explanation: An easement curve is another engineering term for a transition curve, easing the change in curvature and super-elevation between tangents and circular arcs.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Easement curve = Transition curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q71) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Two straights connected using a single arc of constant radius is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: A simple circular curve consists of a single arc of constant radius connecting two intersecting straight tangents.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Single arc of constant radius = Simple circular curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q72) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: In India a curve is designated by
bankQuestions.explanation: In Indian railway and highway engineering practice, curves are designated by their degree of curvature (D) subtended by a standard 30 m or 20 m chord.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Designated by Degree of curve (D ≈ 1719/R for 30m chord).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q73) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is also referred as versed sine of the curve ?
bankQuestions.explanation: The versed sine of a curve is the mid-ordinate (M), which is the perpendicular distance from the center of the long chord to the apex of the curve.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Versed sine of curve = Mid-ordinate M = R(1 - cos(∆/2)).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q89) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the permanent adjustment test checks the perpendicularity between horizontal axis and vertical axis ?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Spire test checks and adjusts the horizontal trunnion axis to be perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spire test = Horizontal axis ⊥ Vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q92) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The most widely used antenna in GPS is
bankQuestions.explanation: Microstrip patch antennas are the most widely used compact GPS antennas due to their low profile, light weight, and circular polarization capability.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Microstrip patch antenna is widely used in GPS receivers.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q85) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The first GPS satellite was launched in
bankQuestions.explanation: The first prototype GPS Block I satellite (Navstar 1) was launched into orbit on February 22, 1978.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First GPS satellite launched in 1978.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q86) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which type of wave is used to operate EDM?
bankQuestions.explanation: Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM) devices transmit modulated electromagnetic waves (infrared, visible laser, or microwave) to measure distances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: EDM uses Electromagnetic waves.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q87) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Data collector is used for total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: In Total Station surveying, the internal electronic data collector records slope distances, horizontal and vertical angles, and point coordinates in digital storage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Data collector keeps digital data records.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q88) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: An EDM based instrument is
bankQuestions.explanation: A Total Station is an integrated electronic instrument combining an electronic theodolite, an EDM, and a microprocessor data collector.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Total Station incorporates EDM.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q29) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Expand GPS
bankQuestions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System, a satellite-based radionavigation system developed by the United States Department of Defense.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Global Positioning System.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q51) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which year does first microprocessor was invented?
bankQuestions.explanation: The world's first single-chip commercial microprocessor, the Intel 4004 (4-bit CPU), was invented and released in 1971 by Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, and Stanley Mazor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First microprocessor (Intel 4004) was invented in 1971.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q66) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the full form of GUI?
bankQuestions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, enabling users to interact with software through visual icons. (In official answer key, option D Geometrical user interface was marked).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Option D marked as per official key.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q67) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the use of function key F3?
bankQuestions.explanation: In AutoCAD drafting, the F3 function key toggles Running Object Snap (OSNAP) on and off.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F3 toggles OSNAP.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q70) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following software is limited for AutoCAD installation?
bankQuestions.explanation: AutoCAD compatibility has evolved; Windows 10 is the supported 64-bit platform while legacy systems are limited/unsupported.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Windows 10 is standard baseline.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q71) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the use of the short cut key M text?
bankQuestions.explanation: In AutoCAD, the command alias 'MTEXT' (or MT) invokes Multiline Text creation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MTEXT = Multi text.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q72) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the full form of UCS?
bankQuestions.explanation: UCS stands for User Coordinate System, allowing drafters to orient X, Y, and Z axes relative to any workplane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: User Coordinate System.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q73) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following pointing device is cheaper while comparing the digitilizer?
bankQuestions.explanation: A computer mouse is an inexpensive, ubiquitous pointing device compared to an electromagnetic digitizer tablet/puck.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mouse is much cheaper than a digitizer puck.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q74) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which short cut key does the work of redo last action?
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard keyboard shortcut to Redo the last undone action in Windows/AutoCAD is Ctrl + Y (while Ctrl + Z is Undo).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl + Y = Redo; Ctrl + Z = Undo.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q75) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Of the following which is the correct input method to draw a line of 100 units at an angle of 40° in anticlockwise direction from positive X axis on a default AutoCAD working space ?
bankQuestions.explanation: In AutoCAD, polar coordinates are input as @distance<angle, so 100 units at 40° anticlockwise from positive X is input as @100<40.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: @distance<angle => @100<40.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q90) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Which function key is used for on/off object snap, while drafting in AutoCAD ?
bankQuestions.explanation: In AutoCAD drafting, the F3 function key toggles Running Object Snap (OSNAP) mode on and off.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F3 = OSNAP.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q97) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The path tracked by a projectile is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The parabolic path described by a projectile moving under the action of gravity in the absence of air resistance is termed its trajectory.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Path of a projectile = Trajectory.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q9) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: π Radians = ___________ grades
bankQuestions.explanation: In the centesimal angle measurement system, 1 right angle = 100 grades (100g). Thus, π radians (180°) = 200 grades.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: π radians = 180° = 200 grades.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q13) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is termed as the quantity of matter contained in a body?
bankQuestions.explanation: Mass is the fundamental scalar quantity of matter contained in a body, which remains invariant regardless of gravitational field.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quantity of matter = Mass.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q89) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: How many watts for 1 horse power in British system?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the British Imperial engineering system, 1 mechanical horsepower (hp) equals 746 Watts (550 ft·lbf/s). Metric hp equals 735.5 W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: British hp = 746 W; Metric hp = 735.5 W.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q90) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the S.I. unit of heat?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the International System of Units (SI), heat energy is measured in Joules (J). Note: In official provisional answer key, Option A Calorie is recorded.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SI unit is Joule; Option A Calorie marked as official key.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q91) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is called for the materials that restricts heat flow by radiation, conduction and convection?
bankQuestions.explanation: Thermal insulators are materials with very low thermal conductivity that resist the transfer of heat by conduction, convection, and radiation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Restricts heat flow = Insulators.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q92) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the term for the object seen higher than eye level?
bankQuestions.explanation: The angle subtended between the horizontal line of sight and the inclined line directed to an object above eye level is the angle of elevation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Above eye level = Angle of elevation. Below eye level = Angle of depression.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q93) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the centre of gravity of a sphere?
bankQuestions.explanation: By spherical symmetry, the center of gravity of a uniform solid sphere lies exactly at its geometric center.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Center of gravity of a sphere is at its center.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q94) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of tempering a steel?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tempering is a heat treatment process performed after hardening to reduce excessive brittleness and relieve internal quenching stresses while maintaining toughness.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tempering reduces brittleness and restores toughness.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q95) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the term used for maximum stress attained by a material before rupture?
bankQuestions.explanation: Ultimate stress (tensile strength) is the maximum nominal stress attained on the engineering stress-strain curve prior to necking and rupture.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Maximum stress before rupture = Ultimate stress.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q96) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Which formula is suitable for the area of a circle, whose diameter is (d)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The area of a circle in terms of its diameter d is Area = π (d/2)² = π d² / 4.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area = πd² / 4.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q97) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the area of irregular shape by Simpson's rule?
bankQuestions.explanation: Simpson's 1/3rd rule for computing area under an odd number of ordinates (even number of intervals h) is Area = (h/3) × [(y1 + yn) + 4(sum of even) + 2(sum of odd)].
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area = (h/3) × [First + Last + 4(Evens) + 2(Odds)].
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q98) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What are the three consecutive numbers if their sum is 42?
bankQuestions.explanation: Let three consecutive integers be x, x+1, x+2. Their sum 3x + 3 = 42 => 3x = 39 => x = 13. The numbers are 13, 14, 15.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q99) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the value of (a⁵)⁷ ?
bankQuestions.explanation: According to the laws of exponents, (a^m)^n = a^(m × n). Thus, (a⁵)⁷ = a^(5 × 7) = a³⁵.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: (a^m)^n = a^(m×n) => (a⁵)⁷ = a³⁵.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q100) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: 1 m = __________ cm.
bankQuestions.explanation: In the metric system, 1 meter = 100 centimeters = 1000 millimeters.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q22) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: 1 hectare = ___________ m².
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 hectare = 100 m × 100 m = 10,000 m² = 10⁴ m².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 hectare = 10,000 m² = 10⁴ m².
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q38) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: 6020 seconds =
bankQuestions.explanation: 6020 seconds / 60 = 100 minutes and 20 seconds. 100 minutes = 1 degree and 40 minutes. Thus, 6020" = 01° 40' 20".
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q78) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Formula for finding area of a plane triangle whose base is b, height h, is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The geometric area of a plane triangle with base b and vertical altitude h is Area = 0.5 × base × height = 0.5 bh.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area = 1/2 × b × h = 0.5 bh.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q98) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: What is the abbreviation for MOEF?
bankQuestions.explanation: MOEF stands for Ministry of Environment and Forests (now MoEFCC: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ministry of Environment and Forests.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q65) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the other name of dwelling unit?
bankQuestions.explanation: A dwelling unit is defined in building bye-laws and the National Building Code (NBC) as a residential building or apartment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dwelling unit = Residential building.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q68) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: What is the normal life period of residential building with concrete roof according to NBC 2005?
bankQuestions.explanation: According to NBC 2005 / IS 456, the design life period for monumental and permanent residential buildings with reinforced concrete roofs is 100 years.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 100 years for permanent RCC buildings.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q69) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The standard size of brick
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard modular size of a common building brick as per BIS IS 1077 is 19 cm × 9 cm × 9 cm (nominal size with mortar is 20 × 10 × 10 cm).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard/modular = 19 × 9 × 9 cm. Nominal = 20 × 10 × 10 cm.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q76) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The central part of the tree is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The innermost core/central portion of a tree stem is the pith (or medulla), which supplies nutrients to young saplings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Innermost core = Pith (Medulla).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q77) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Weight of 1 bag of cement
bankQuestions.explanation: As per Indian Standard IS 1489 / IS 269, a standard commercial bag of Portland cement weighs exactly 50 kg (volume ≈ 34.7 liters).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q78) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Chemically which rock is calcarious rock?
bankQuestions.explanation: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from recrystallized limestone/dolomite, whose primary chemical constituent is calcium carbonate (calcarious rock).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Calcareous rocks: Marble, Limestone. Siliceous: Granite, Basalt. Argillaceous: Slate, Laterite.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q79) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the
bankQuestions.explanation: Vicat's apparatus with standard plunger and needles is used to determine the standard consistency, initial setting time, and final setting time of cement paste.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Consistency (10 mm plunger), Initial setting (1 mm needle), Final setting (collar needle).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 43/2023 (Q80) • Tracer / Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The structure which is used to carry canal over natural drain is called
bankQuestions.explanation: An aqueduct is a cross-drainage structure in which the irrigation canal is carried in a flume supported on piers completely over a natural stream/drain.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Canal over drain = Aqueduct. Drain over canal = Superpassage.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q65) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Area of land irrigated divided by the unit volume of irrigation water is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Duty is defined as the area of land (in hectares) that can be irrigated by a continuous discharge of 1 cumec of water throughout the base period.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area per unit discharge = Duty (hectares/cumec).
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q93) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Portion of a brick made by cutting across it lengthwise into exactly two parts is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: A queen closer is formed by cutting a standard brick lengthwise into two equal halves.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cut lengthwise = Queen closer. Cut widthwise = Bat. Triangle cut from corner = King closer.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q94) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: When the bed level of canal and drainage is at the same level, is provided.
bankQuestions.explanation: When the bed levels of a canal and a natural drainage stream intersect at the exact same level, a level crossing with regulator gates is provided.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Canal and drain at same bed level = Level crossing.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q96) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: Main constituent of portland cement is
bankQuestions.explanation: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO, 60-67%) is the primary chemical constituent of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), followed by silica (17-25%).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lime (CaO, ~63%) is the major constituent of cement.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q99) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: In , headers and stretchers are laid alternatively in the same course.
bankQuestions.explanation: In a Flemish bond, alternate stretchers and headers are laid in the same course, with queen closers placed next to quoin headers in alternating courses.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Alternate headers and stretchers in same course = Flemish bond. Alternate courses of headers and stretchers = English bond.
bankQuestions.examName: Paper 106/2017 (Q100) • Surveyor Gr. II (KWA)

bankQuestions.question: The command used to join two non - parallel lines by drawing a bevelled line
bankQuestions.explanation: The CHAMFER command (alias CHA) connects two non-parallel lines by drawing an angled beveled line between them based on specified chamfer distances or angle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CHAMFER creates beveled straight angled corners; FILLET creates rounded tangent arcs.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Command used to remove the selected object from a drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: The ERASE command (alias E) deletes selected objects from the drawing database. Deleted objects can be retrieved using OOPS or UNDO.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ERASE (E) removes entities. OOPS restores entities deleted by the most recent ERASE command.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What happens when a user presses Ctrl+3 in his AutoCAD ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + 3 opens and closes the Tool Palettes window. Tool palettes provide organized tabs of reusable blocks, hatch patterns, and custom CAD tools.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl+1 = Properties, Ctrl+2 = DesignCenter, Ctrl+3 = Tool Palettes, Ctrl+4 = Sheet Set Manager.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following file extensions cannot open in AutoCAD ?
bankQuestions.explanation: .dot is a Microsoft Word document template extension and cannot be opened in AutoCAD. AutoCAD opens .dwg (drawing), .dxf (exchange format), and .dws (standards).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: AutoCAD native drawing format is .dwg, template is .dwt, exchange is .dxf, backup is .bak.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: _____ is the short cut key of Block edit :
bankQuestions.explanation: BE (BEDIT) is the shortcut command for Block Edit, which opens the selected block definition in the in-place Block Editor environment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: B = BLOCK (create block), BE = BEDIT (edit block), W = WBLOCK (write block to file).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: How many workspaces are available in AutoCAD ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard AutoCAD provides 3 core workspaces: Drafting & Annotation (2D), 3D Basics, and 3D Modeling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Workspaces configure the ribbon and toolbar layout suited for 2D drafting or 3D modeling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is a volatile memory ?
bankQuestions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile primary memory that loses all its stored data when power is switched off. ROM, PROM, and EPROM retain data permanently.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: RAM is volatile (temporary read/write memory); ROM is non-volatile (permanent).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: In Auto CAD, the key stroke used for the function 'redo' :
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + Y is the standard key combination to Redo an action that was previously cancelled by Undo in AutoCAD and Windows applications.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl+Z = Undo, Ctrl+Y = Redo, Ctrl+S = Save, Ctrl+O = Open.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the key for 3D OSNAP?
bankQuestions.explanation: Function key F4 toggles 3D Object Snap (3D OSNAP) mode, enabling precision snapping to 3D vertices, edges, face centers, and knot points on solids.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F3 = 2D OSNAP; F4 = 3D OSNAP.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Offset command can be used for drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: The OFFSET command (alias O) creates parallel lines, parallel curves, or concentric circles at a specified offset distance or through a given point.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OFFSET is the most frequently used command for creating wall thicknesses and road boundaries.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The command used to erase the object partly is :
bankQuestions.explanation: The TRIM command (alias TR) erases part of an object extending beyond cutting boundaries, leaving the rest of the object intact.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TRIM requires cutting edges; ERASE removes the entire selected entity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The memory which is programmed at the time of manufacturing is
bankQuestions.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) is permanently programmed with bootstrap firmware by the manufacturer during IC fabrication and cannot be modified.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ROM contains the BIOS program needed to boot the computer hardware.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: _____ command is used to show the section of solids or objects
bankQuestions.explanation: The HATCH command (alias H) fills an enclosed area or section plane of an object with standard cross-hatching patterns to represent cut sections.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard hatching pattern for generic sectional views is ANSI31 (45° parallel lines).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is compiler?
bankQuestions.explanation: A compiler is system software that converts source code written in a high-level programming language into machine-executable binary code all at once.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compiler translates the whole program at once; Interpreter translates and runs line-by-line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The short key for removes italic format for selected text is :
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + I toggles italic styling on and off for selected text in AutoCAD MTEXT and word processors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl+B = Bold, Ctrl+I = Italic, Ctrl+U = Underline.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which command used for drafting smooth irregular curve and shapes that are difficult to draw as arc?
bankQuestions.explanation: The SPLINE command (alias SPL) generates smooth, irregular, non-circular polynomial curves passing through or near control points, ideal for contours.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In topographical surveying, SPLINE is the standard command used to trace contour lines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the term that marking the drawing objects on a layer permanent and non - editable?
bankQuestions.explanation: Locking a layer ensures that objects on that layer remain visible and snappable for reference, but cannot be accidentally edited, moved, or deleted.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Locked layers are visible but protected from modification; Frozen layers are invisible and excluded from regeneration.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which command convert discrete object into polyline
bankQuestions.explanation: The JOIN command (alias J) connects touching lines, arcs, or polylines sharing common endpoints into a single continuous polyline.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lines must share exact contiguous endpoints to be combined using JOIN.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The fillet command in AutoCAD creates
bankQuestions.explanation: The FILLET command (alias F) rounds the corners of two intersecting lines or segments by constructing a tangent circular arc of specified radius.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FILLET with Radius = 0 creates sharp 90-degree corners quickly.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: How many points do you need to define for the rectangle command ?
bankQuestions.explanation: The RECTANGLE command (alias REC) requires 2 diagonally opposite corner points (first corner and other corner) to construct the rectangle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: AutoCAD draws rectangles as closed 4-segment 2D polylines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What happens when a user presses Ctrl+1 in his AutoCAD ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Pressing Ctrl + 1 toggles the Properties Palette, which allows viewing and editing layer, color, linetype, scale, and geometric coordinates of selected objects.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl + 1 is the universal Properties shortcut in AutoCAD.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Data stored in primary storage is represented using
bankQuestions.explanation: Primary computer storage (RAM) stores information using binary digits (bits: 0 and 1), which is represented mathematically in Base 2.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Base 2 = Binary (0,1); Base 8 = Octal; Base 10 = Decimal; Base 16 = Hexadecimal.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following pointing device is cheaper while comparing the digitizer?
bankQuestions.explanation: A mouse is a mass-produced, inexpensive optical pointing device compared to expensive digitizer boards and pucks used in professional cartography.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Digitizers and pucks are high-precision cartographic input devices.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The shortcut key to extend a selection to the end of a word is :
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Right Arrow extends text selection word by word to the right until the end of the selected word.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Shift+Arrow selects characters; adding Ctrl moves the selection boundary by whole words.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: A pattern of dots that appear on AutoCAD screen of computer but not visible on print is called;
bankQuestions.explanation: The GRID (F7) is a visible pattern of reference dots or lines covering the drawing limits on the screen, but it never appears on plotted/printed drawings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F7 toggles GRID; F9 toggles SNAP. Grid dots are purely on-screen visual references.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The computer language 'C' is an example for :
bankQuestions.explanation: 'C' is a high-level programming language developed by Dennis Ritchie in 1972 at Bell Laboratories for system and application programming.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Machine code is 1st gen, Assembly is 2nd gen, C/C++/Java are high-level languages.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Some CAD programs have a command line, this is where (a/an) _____ can be typed to activate it.
bankQuestions.explanation: The Command Line is the dedicated interface prompt where command names or shortcut aliases are typed to invoke AutoCAD drafting operations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pressing Enter or Spacebar at the command line executes typed commands or repeats the last command.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Example for an operating system is
bankQuestions.explanation: Microsoft Windows is an operating system that manages system hardware, file storage, and software processes. COBOL, BASIC, and C++ are programming languages.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OS controls hardware resources; examples: Windows, Linux, Unix, macOS, Android.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: A network of computers and other devices that is confined to a relatively small space is called
bankQuestions.explanation: A LAN (Local Area Network) is a computer network confined to a geographically small area like a room, office, home, or campus.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: LAN = Local Area Network; MAN = Metropolitan Area Network; WAN = Wide Area Network.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which command is used to divide the object into 'n' number of segments having equal lengths?
bankQuestions.explanation: The DIVIDE command creates point objects or blocks spaced at equal distances along the length or perimeter of an object into a specified number of segments.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIVIDE creates N equal segments; MEASURE places points at fixed length intervals.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the full form of GUI?
bankQuestions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, enabling users to interact with software through graphical icons, windows, and visual menus rather than typed text commands.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CLI = Command Line Interface; GUI = Graphical User Interface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: The command for polygon is _____ in AutoCAD
bankQuestions.explanation: POL is the standard command alias for POLYGON in AutoCAD, used to draw regular polygons with 3 to 1024 equal sides inscribed or circumscribed about a circle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: POL = POLYGON, PL = PLINE, PO = POINT.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD which one of the following is a modifying command?
bankQuestions.explanation: ROTATE (alias RO) is a modify command used to rotate objects around a specified base point. ZOOM and REDO are viewing and editing utilities.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Draw commands create entities; Modify commands (Move, Rotate, Scale, Trim) alter them.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — AutoCAD & CADD Bank
